articles.title: Estrella: DAR moving ‘full speed’ to split collective land titles
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said on Thursday his agency is “moving full speed ahead” in breaking up collective land titles as the World Bank-financed project…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said on Thursday his agency is “moving full speed ahead” in breaking up collective land titles as the World Bank-financed project nears expiry.

The Support to Parcelization of Lands for Individual Titling (SPLIT) project is an initiative by the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) partly funded by the World Bank – that aims to break up collective land titles covering 1.38 million hectares issued to over a million agrarian reform beneficiaries.
At a congressional budget hearing, Estrella said there are about 750,000 Collective Certificate of Land Ownership Awards (CCLOA) pending before DAR as the loan is set to expire in Dec. 2027.
“We might make it at 500 [thousand], or a little less, for this year, and then finish the entire thing by next year,” he told lawmakers.
Estrella said the project “is still a priority” of DAR, as he touted that his agency is “one of the best, if not the best, agencies implementing World Bank-funded projects.”
Speaking to the Inquirer after the hearing, the agrarian reform secretary said breaking up CCLOAs “is easy.”
“If it were only up to us, we would finish this right now,” he said in Filipino. “It’s the World Bank slowing things down because they are strict in the use of funds.”
Land reform is a contentious issue in the Philippines, an agricultural country where vestiges of Spanish colonial land ownership have endured for decades, concentrating land possession among a few.
About 47 percent of the country’s total land area is agricultural land, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. /mr

articles.title: NBI confirms Chuangxing rebars used in collapsed Pampanga building
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Steel bars recovered from the rubble of a collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga, were traced to a steel manufacturing plant under investigation, the National Bureau of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Steel bars recovered from the rubble of a collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga, were traced to a steel manufacturing plant under investigation, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said Thursday.

The disclosure was made during the Senate Committee on Economic Affairs’ second hearing on the domestic steel industry, where lawmakers continued to examine the possible use of substandard steel products in buildings and other structures.
Sen. Risa Hontiveros, who chairs the panel, asked whether the bureau could confirm that the steel bars recovered from the collapsed Pampanga building indeed came from Chuangxing Steel Inc.
NBI Senior Agent, lawyer Zulikha Marie Conales confirmed the finding.
“We confirm, we were able to recover rebars from the rubbles of the (collapsed) building in Pampanga, Madam Chair,” she said.

The confirmation came amid ongoing investigation into allegations that Chuangxing, a Chinese-owned steel plant in Magalang, Pampanga, may have produced and distributed alleged substandard steel bars to different parts of the country and were later used in construction.
Chuangxing was raided and shut down on July 18 after authorities discovered allegedly substandard steel products and radioactive materials inside the facility.
The raid came weeks after the May 24 collapse of a nine-story building under construction in Barangay Balibago, which left 27 dead.

Hontiveros also asked Conales about reports that 70 percent of the defective steel used in a damaged building in Mindanao came from Sanjia, another steel manufacturing plant under scrutiny by authorities.
“We confirm, madam chair,” Conales said, referring to the NBI’s investigation of the site.

The NBI had earlier raided Sanjia’s 22.6-hectare plant at the Phividec Industrial Estate in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, where radioactive materials were found, prompting the temporary shutdown of the facility.
Hontiveros said the NBI’s findings raised concerns about where else the alleged substandard steel may have been used.
“Grabe po yun because then we need to think about saan pa napunta yung ibang ganoong klaseng substandard na products, saan pang ibang mga gusali dito sa ating bansa,” she said.
(That is alarming because then we need to think about where else those kinds of substandard products went, and what other buildings here in our country they may have been used in.) /dp

articles.title: Senate may revisit impeachment voting threshold amid changes in composition --Zubiri
articles.summary: Senator Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri said some senators are seeking to revisit the voting threshold for the impeachment case, citing changes in the composition of the Senate since the required vote was…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 9:51pm

Senator Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri said some senators are seeking to revisit the voting threshold for the impeachment case, citing changes in the composition of the Senate since the required vote was set.

“There were some colleagues who want to revisit because at that time wala pa yung mga nawawalang senador ngayon kasi may nasa kulungan, isa at large. I think that is the issue,” Zubiri told reporters in a press conference on Thursday.
(There were some colleagues who want to revisit it because at that time, the senators who are now absent were still there—one is detained and one is at large. I think that is the issue.)
Asked if there were proposals to lower the threshold, Zubiri answered:
“Yes,” he said, noting some senators have concerns about the threshold, but when asked when it would be debated, he deferred to the presiding officer.
“Best person to answer is PO (presiding officer)," he said.
He also said he expects the issue could eventually be brought before the Supreme Court
“I’m sure someone will take it to the Supreme Court,” he added.
He further stressed that the matter should be debated publicly.

Meanwhile, Zubiri also defended the Senate’s decision to allow budget hearings to run alongside plenary sessions, saying the chamber would not be able to complete its workload if the proceedings were kept to the usual schedule.
The Senate is currently juggling three major activities: the impeachment trial, the 2027 budget process and its legislative agenda.

He said the Senate amended its rules to allow senators attending budget hearings during plenary hours to be recognized as present. The arrangement is intended to maximize the chamber’s working time and prevent delays in the approval of the national budget.
He noted that the Senate is targeting completion of the budget deliberations by October so that plenary action can proceed in November and the country can avoid a reenacted budget.
Zubiri said that without the simultaneous budget hearings and plenary work, the Senate could still have 12 departments left to tackle by October 23, based on Senator Joel Villanueva's estimate.
“Pagod na pagod”
Zubiri also acknowledged the strain of the Senate’s unusually heavy workload.
“I’m very candid so I just tell them how I feel. I’m just being honest. It doesn’t matter kung pagod na pagod na ako. If we have to work 24/7, we will work.”
(It doesn’t matter if I’m extremely tired. If we have to work 24/7, we will work.)

He said the remark reflected his candid assessment of the workload, noting that it is the first time the Senate has had to handle the impeachment proceedings, budget deliberations and legislative agenda simultaneously. He added that senators may not get their usual October break as they work to meet the demands of the impeachment case and the budget. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: UK mortgage borrowers brace for rate jump amid global bond sell-off
articles.summary: Swap rates rise to three-year high as increase in oil prices leads to fears of higher inflation

blocks.text: Homeowners in the UK are braced for a jump in mortgage rates, driven by higher inflation and interest rate increase expectations amid turmoil in the global bond markets.
UK swap rates, which lenders use to price mortgages, have risen to a three-year high, as this week’s global bond market sell-off ripples through the economy.
The five-year swap rate rose above 4.52% on Wednesday, the highest level since October 2023. This is expected to result in higher interest rates on fixed-term mortgages.

A jump in oil prices as the US and Iran exchanged fire this week for the first time in a month has led to fears of higher inflation, leading investors to sell bonds, which pushes up their yield, or interest rate. The moves in gilts, as UK government bonds are known as, have been bigger than those in other countries.

Coventry Building Society has become the first mainstream lender to increase mortgage rates. It raised rates across its entire range of fixed-rate mortgages for new and existing residential and buy-to-let borrowers.

blocks.caption: Fixed-year mortgage rates were unchanged on Thursday. Photograph: Amer Ghazzal/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Although the turmoil in the bond markets eased on Thursday, the consequences of the jump in bond yields could be serious for borrowers.
That is because UK swap rates – the interest rates that banks charge when they borrow from each other – have been pushed up by the rise in gilt yields.

Russ Mould, the investment director at the trading platform AJ Bell, said: “Credit card, mortgage and auto loan interest rates will rise if bond yields rise, as the lenders seek to preserve loan book margins and manage their risk.”
If the cost of government borrowing continues to remain high, it could undermine Andy Burnham’s efforts to ease cost of living pressures.

The new prime minister attempted to calm volatile bond markets on Wednesday, using his first appearance at prime minister’s questions to promise decisions for the autumn budget would be “grounded in fiscal responsibility”.

He spoke as the yield on UK 10-year government debt hit its highest level since 2008 for a second day, before retreating thanks to a drop in the oil price. On Thursday, Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, dipped 0.6% to $95 a barrel.
after newsletter promotion

Oil has been one of the key factors driving the bond market sell-off, as inflationary pressures from high prices could force central banks to raise interest rates, along with worries over high government spending. Government bonds are also competing with a flurry of corporate debt issuance by technology companies keen to fund their spending on AI infrastructure.

Tom Simpson, the managing director of homes at Yorkshire Building Society, said swap rates were now 0.7% above where they were a year ago, but there was “much more volatility” in March, at the start of the Iran war.

“All things being equal, you would expect a modest increase in mortgage rates based on what we’ve seen so far,” he told the BBC, advising people who were worried about this to speak to an independent mortgage adviser.

“When there is a movement in the market, that can pull forward demand. People will try to lock those rates in.” However, he added that the 0.1 percentage point increase over the past week was below the 0.5 percentage point increase in the 10 days after the US and Israel first launched airstrikes on Tehran.
Fixed-year mortgage rates were unchanged on Thursday, according to the latest figures from Moneyfacts. The average two-year fix is 5.59%, while a typical five-year fixed deal costs 5.63%.

articles.title: ‘Supersized’ El Niño may become strongest ever recorded, UN says
articles.summary: 'El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up,' says United Nations chief Antonio Guterres

blocks.text: EL NIÑO. A ship transits the Panama Canal near the Gamboa hydrometeorological monitoring station as a lack of rainfall linked to El Nino affects the water levels, in Gamboa, Panama, on August 27, 2026.
Enea Lebrun/Reuters
'El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up,' says United Nations chief Antonio Guterres

items: The El Niño phenomenon is expected to intensify through 2027, potentially becoming the strongest on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization.
There is a near 100% likelihood that El Niño will persist until February 2027, driven by exceptionally warm Pacific Ocean temperatures, which could lead to extreme weather events globally.
The WMO is enhancing preparedness and early warning systems to help countries manage the impacts of El Niño, including potential food crises and shifts in global temperature patterns.

GENEVA, Switzerland – The El Niño weather phenomenon is set to intensify further into 2027 and could be the strongest ever, raising risks of extreme weather into next year, the World Meteorological Organization said on Thursday, September 3.

The UN weather agency said its forecasts showed a near 100% likelihood that El Niño would persist through February 2027, fueled by exceptionally warm Pacific Ocean temperatures. This is the first time it has expressed such a degree of certainty, the WMO said.
“If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began. So literally off the charts,” WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo told a Geneva press conference.

El Niño is a periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific caused by weakening trade winds. It occurs every two to seven years and tends to last up to 12 months, causing intense rains and droughts across Latin America.
A very strong El Niño can significantly shift rainfall and temperature patterns worldwide, and fuel extreme weather, such as droughts and typhoons.
While it is a naturally occurring phenomenon and not directly linked to fossil fuel-driven climate change, it can be intensified by warmer ocean temperatures, which are.
“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: The planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up,” said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.

Sample Pacific Ocean temperatures in this year’s El Niño — one of just four categorized in the top “very strong” bracket in records dating back to 1950 — are already more than 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit) above normal, the WMO said.
The event has already had an impact on soft commodities in tropical areas, causing a severe food crisis across Central America’s Dry Corridor.

It is set to peak towards the end of this year, the WMO said in a statement. But its effects will continue into 2027 and are set to leave higher global temperatures next year in its wake, WMO officials said.

“Normally after an El Niño event we tend to see a pulse in the global temperatures — a temporary one,” Wilfran Moufouma Okia, the WMO’s chief of climate prediction services, told reporters, referring to 2024, which was the hottest year so far. “2027 has the potential to be the warmest on record.”
The WMO said it was stepping up preparedness and early warning efforts in preparation to allow states to take early action, such as switching to drought-resistant crops in some places.

“WMO is committed to working closely with partners across the United Nations and humanitarian system to provide the climate intelligence and insights needed to support disaster management and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water resources,” Saulo said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sandiganbayan affirms junking of Jinggoy Estrada’s bail bid
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Left “unconvinced” with the invocation of former Senate President Juan Ponce Enrile’s “exceptional circumstance,” the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Thursday…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Left “unconvinced” with the invocation of former Senate President Juan Ponce Enrile’s “exceptional circumstance,” the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Thursday affirmed its earlier ruling which blocked the move of Sen. Jinggoy Estrada for temporary freedom.
Estrada on Aug. 3 filed a motion for reconsideration (MR) on the anti-graft court’s resolution denying his motion to fix bail even without a hearing.

“The motion for reconsideration is DENIED,” said the six-page resolution penned by Associate Justice Gener Gito “After a careful review of accused Estrada’s arguments, the court finds no compelling reason to depart from its ruling.”

In support of his position, Estrada cited the Supreme Court decision on Enrile vs Sandiganbayan case in 2015 to allow the late senator to post bail in his plunder case without a bail hearing at that time.
“The Supreme Court held that Senator Enrile was entitled to bail regardless of the strength of the evidence against him because he was not a flight risk,” stated the 13-page MR of Estrada.
Estrada’s motion said he is “similarly situated” with Enrile in a sense that both of them were not flight risk.
“Accused Estrada once again places heavy reliance on the Enrile ruling,” the resolution said. “The court remains unconvinced.”
According to the court, the circumstances of Enrile and Estrada are “materially different.”
“The Supreme Court considered, among others, Senator Juan Ponce Enrile’s advanced age and fragile state of health, together with other circumstances demonstrating
that his continued detention posed serious humanitarian concern,” the resolution said.
“No comparable circumstance involving advanced age, frail health, or any other compelling humanitarian consideration similar to those present in Enrile has been shown,” it added.

Estrada is facing plunder case stemming from alleged “intricate mechanism involving illegal budgetary insertions and project allocations” within the Department of Public Works and Highways’ infrastructure portfolio for fiscal year 2025 worth P573 million, according to prosecutors.
The senator has repeatedly denied the accusations.
Also on Thursday, Estrada refused to enter a plea during his arraignment, when the formal reading of his charges was read to him, prompting the court to enter a not guilty plea on his behalf. /mr

articles.title: DFA aims to roll out next-gen PH passports by 2028
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) is aiming to roll out its next-generation Philippine passports by 2028. DFA policy planning and coordination Assistant Secretary…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) is aiming to roll out its next-generation Philippine passports by 2028.
DFA policy planning and coordination Assistant Secretary Robespierre Bolivar made this pronouncement at the House of Representatives appropriations committee hearing on the department’s 2027 budget.

“We are hoping to redesign the passport booklet to make it fully compliant with ICAO and with enhanced security features, additional pages for a full 10-year validity and the latest contactless chip technology,” Bolivar told lawmakers.

“The estimated indicative launch of the next generation e-passport is June 2028, but over the next year, we would need to phase in the requirements we need for the rollout of the next generation passport,” he noted.
DFA is seeking P35.173 billion for 2027, of which P5.8 billion will fund the next-generation passport program.
Earlier in the hearing, Bolivar reported that the agency issued around 1.57 million passports with at least 35 iterations of the department’s “Passport on Wheels” program as of last August 31.

He also noted that the agency issued 67,697 visas and electronic visas; 413,597 apostille certificates and electronic apostille certificates; and 36,354 civil registry reports in 2026 so far, maintaining at least 42 consular offices nationwide. /mr

articles.title: Pampanga helps ease floods at NLEx, tallies monsoon damage at P1.339B
articles.summary: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — The Pampanga provincial government and the provincial chapter of League of Municipalities of the Philippines on Thursday (Sept. 3) wrapped up their efforts in…

blocks.text: CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, Pampanga — The Pampanga provincial government and the provincial chapter of League of Municipalities of the Philippines on Thursday (Sept. 3) wrapped up their efforts in easing floods on the San Simon segments of the North Luzon Expressway, where motorists were caught in gridlocks for up to 8 hours over the weekend.
Three dump trucks of sand and 1,500 sand bags were provided by the province, and close to 50 people were mobilized to redirect or siphon out floodwaters until Wednesday midnight.
The costs of damages on crops, fisheries, machineries and farm structures reached P1.339 billion, the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office said.
Vice Governor Dennis Pineda lent two machineries to pump out floodwater.

“We did our bit to hasten the flow of traffic to be able to minimize the disruptions to motorists and passengers, and the economy,” the vice governor said as Pampanga continues to struggle with the impact of constant rains brought by the monsoon and a series of weather disturbances.

On Thursday morning, the San Fernando-Santo Tomas-Minalin Tail Dike took on another damage, with a 60-meter section collapsing in Barangay San Nicolas in Minalin town, Mayor Philip Naguit reported in a live broadcast on social media.

Naguit said the damaged segment was part of the 100-meter eroded shoulder discovered by Vice Gov. Pineda in July, adding that the Department of Public Works and Highways stopped repairs when heavy monsoon rains began lashing out by mid-August.

This was the ninth damage that the tail dike sustained, the most serious being a 30-meter breach on August 29 when the Gugu Creek overflowed and rerouted to the San Francisco River. Strong currents washed away the check gate there.

As of Thurday, 256 villages in 18 towns remained flooded but water levels on downstream Pampanga River rose to critical levels, according to the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.

The floods have affected 374,292 families or 1.204 million individuals, with 8,964 families (32,461individuals) remaining in 456 evacuation centers. At least 3,538 families (14,843 individuals) are being served outside evacuation sites. So far, the costs of assistance from government and private groups reached P191.5 million. /mr

articles.title: Hillary Clinton leads tributes to Gloria Steinem: ‘Her activism was rooted in optimism’
articles.summary: Former US secretary of state joins Roxane Gay, Rachel Cargle and others in heralding groundbreaking feminist

blocks.text: Hillary Clinton led tributes to Gloria Steinem on Thursday, hailing the American feminist icon who died at 92 at home in New York as “one of the architects of the entire structure of women’s equality”.

Clinton, a former US secretary of state, presidential candidate and first lady, appeared on the CBS Mornings TV show to deliver a tribute, urging younger generations to use Steinem as a role model in supporting each other in promoting the causes she championed.
“I’m hoping that young women realize that the fight is worth it,” she said. “It is exhilarating.”

Steinem supported Clinton’s 2016 presidential campaign as the Democratic nominee running against Donald Trump, which was ultimately unsuccessful. Clinton said on Thursday she was “heartsick” at news of the death of her friend and ally.
“Everyone who not only knew her but followed her, was inspired and challenged by her,” she said.

“I think back to my first awareness of Gloria way back in the 1960s into the 70s, when all of a sudden this incredibly smart, beautiful, talented woman began talking about how women should have equal opportunity, how we should aim for the stars, be able to pursue our own dreams.
“I knew there were, back when I was a young woman, schools that wouldn’t take women, jobs that wouldn’t take women, scholarships that weren’t open to women. I lived it.
“But the lived experience became much more real and applicable to our entire society when Gloria began to point it out.”
Clinton noted Steinem’s distaste at what politics had become in recent years, and said she had “the most incredible conversation” with her during a visit to Steinem’s home last year.

“Even though we’re facing some challenges and pushback here in this country and around the world to women’s full participation and equality, Gloria was at heart an optimist,” she said. “Her activism was rooted in optimism, and that’s a moral choice, and she made it every day.”
Others who paid tribute on Thursday recalled Steinem’s trailblazing.

“Gloria was one of a kind. Genuine, generous, curious, thoughtful. She lived a staggering life and her passing is a staggering loss tempered only by the ferocity of her legacy,” Roxane Gay, the prominent social commentator and author of Bad Feminist, commented on the Instagram post announcing Steinem’s death.

Social justice activist Rachel Cargle posted: “Gloria, you changed my life. You seeded a fire in me that would result in my own activism. I am forever grateful to have learned from what you offered the world.”
The veteran journalist Ann Curry, who overcame prolific newsroom misogyny early in her career to become one of the US’s most respected broadcasters, also used the post to remember her friend.

“Thank you Gloria,” she wrote. “You once told me in an interview that it was your mother’s suffering that first moved you to take action for the rights of women. May you now be in her embrace. How the lives of so many shine a little brighter because you were in this world. With respect.”
Christiane Amanpour, an award-winning former war correspondent and now chief international anchor for CNN, posted her tribute on X.
“Gloria Steinem will go down in history as one of the most important activists of all time, leading a movement for the equality of half the world: its women,” Amanpour wrote.

“She lived a long and passionate life dedicated to this vital and basic cause. She did it with intellectual precision, emotional awareness, humor and beauty. May she rest in peace and may the cause thrive.”

Clinton added on Thursday, speaking with CBS: “I think about all of the ways that I saw in my own life, over the course of about 10 to 15 years, Gloria’s pushing on those doors to finally get them open, not only for her to walk through, but for her to lead literally millions of others.
“With all of the setbacks that we’ve seen over the last decade or so, I want her voice to remain in our heads.”

articles.title: Nvidia to buy developer platform Hugging Face in $12.9bn deal
articles.summary:
Semi-conductor giant bets that support for open AI models could offset potential slowdown in demand for chips

Nvidia will buy the popular developer platform Hugging Face for nearly $13bn,…

blocks.text: Nvidia will buy the popular developer platform Hugging Face for nearly $13bn, betting that support for ⁠open AI models could offset a potential slowdown in demand for the semiconductor giant’s chips.
Shares ⁠in Nvidia were ⁠slightly lower ​after the $12.93bn (£9.57bn) deal – which ranks among its biggest ever – was announced for the database of AI models on Thursday.

The New York-based startup Hugging Face, which is backed by Intel, Advanced Micro Devices and Amazon, was founded in 2016 by the French entrepreneurs Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf.
The chipmaker is already a major open AI player in the US with ⁠its widely used Nemotron model and vocal support for the technology.

Acquiring Hugging Face will give it direct access to a platform developers use to ⁠collaborate, test and share tools, potentially providing insight and data that could help it narrow the ​technology gap with top American and ‌Chinese labs.

Demand for open-weight models ‌has surged from businesses balking at the steep bill of deploying the technology. Chinese companies ‌such as DeepSeek and Z.ai have emerged as crucial players with models that can match the best from the US in tasks including generating computer code at a lower cost.
There are fears that some US firms could become reliant on Beijing’s models even as both countries race to dominate a technology they see as crucial to their future.

“Hugging ‌Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem,” said Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, adding that his company’s chips would not be required to ​build on or deploy through Hugging Face.
Under the deal, Nvidia will pay about $11.9bn to Hugging Face investors, while offering an equity-based retention programme of up to $1bn for employees who join Nvidia.
after newsletter promotion

For Nvidia, building up its open source business may help it cushion a demand slowdown from customers such as ⁠Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft, which are developing their own AI chips to cut reliance ​on its costly and ​supply constrained processors.

Hugging Face has also been ​in the news recently after a hack by rogue AI agents that ​escaped OpenAI’s testing ‌environment. Beyond hosting AI ​models, it offers datasets, ​software libraries and cloud services used to build and deploy AI applications.
