articles.title: DepEd to propose new rules on class suspensions, resumptions
articles.summary: Education Secretary Sonny Angara will submit to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. a proposed executive order (EO) that would overhaul the rules on class suspensions and resumptions, after the measure…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 8:24pm

Education Secretary Sonny Angara will submit to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. a proposed executive order (EO) that would overhaul the rules on class suspensions and resumptions, after the measure was approved by the Social Development Committee Cabinet Cluster on Thursday.

The proposed EO seeks to update the framework under Executive Order No. 66, series of 2012, by giving local officials and school heads greater authority to make site-specific decisions while preserving learner safety and minimizing unnecessary learning disruptions.
The proposed policy comes amid significant instructional losses caused by weather disturbances and disasters.

According to data presented to the Cabinet Cluster, basic education institutions lost up to 53 of 180 school days during School Year 2023-2024 because of weather-related and disaster-related class cancellations.
From June 8 to August 31, 2026, some schools also recorded 20 to 40 days of instructional loss, highlighting the need for a more flexible approach to suspensions and resumptions.
Angara said learner safety would remain the government’s priority, but learning continuity must also be protected.

“When a hazard strikes, the safety of our students, teachers, and school personnel is non-negotiable. However, every unnecessary day a classroom stays closed costs our learners their potential and compromises our long-term economic productivity.”
Three-tiered system proposed
The proposed EO would establish three decision-making mechanisms:

items: Automatic suspensions based on national technical thresholds;
Localized suspensions determined by local chief executives; and
Granular, school-level suspensions and resumptions, allowing school heads to make site-specific decisions based on actual conditions, subject to the required coordination and concurrence.

blocks.text: The policy would also expand the hazards covered beyond typhoons to include heavy rainfall, flooding, earthquakes, storm surges, poor air quality, volcanic smog, volcanic hazards, and extreme heat reaching a heat index of 40°C or higher.
Under the proposal, school heads would retain authority to suspend in-person classes based on documented site-specific assessments, with the concurrence of their Schools Division Superintendent.

The measure would also allow schools to resume in-person classes based on site-specific assessments once hazards have cleared. For public schools, the school head would need concurrence from the local chief executive; private basic education schools may declare resumptions in prompt coordination with the local chief executive.
Learning continuity to continue during disruptions

The proposed policy would also formally institutionalize alternative ways of delivering instruction when in-person classes are disrupted, including alternative learning delivery modalities, flexible learning options, self-learning resources, and temporary learning spaces.
Angara said the proposed framework would give local officials and school heads greater flexibility to respond to actual conditions on the ground.
“Under President Marcos’ leadership, we are reframing our approach: we are not merely suspending classes; we are safeguarding learning continuity.”

“By institutionalizing granular suspensions and resumptions, we give our local executives and school heads the legal backing and flexibility to make science-backed decisions tailored to real-time, ground conditions.”

The proposed EO will provide the overarching policy framework, while specific technical thresholds and operational guidelines will be contained in a separate Joint Memorandum Circular to be jointly issued with the Commission on Higher Education, Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, Department of the Interior and Local Government, and Department of Science and Technology. The policy was formulated following consultations with local chief executives, school heads, teachers, parents, and learners. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: DOJ: Minor faces multiple murder charges over Tacloban school shooting
articles.summary: Three counts of murder and two counts of attempted murder are filed against the 15-year-old student

blocks.text: TRAGEDY. San Jose National High School after a shooting incident that left three students dead and 11 others injured, on June 22, 2026.
PIA Tacloban
Three counts of murder and two counts of attempted murder are filed against the 15-year-old student

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Justice (DOJ) filed multiple murder charges against the 15-year-old student tagged in the June 22 school shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City which killed three students and injured 20 others.

Following the inquest proceedings on July 13, Tacloban City prosecutors filed three counts of murder and two counts of attempted murder against the 15-year-old boy before the Family Court of Tacloban City Regional Trial Court on July 13, the DOJ announced on Thursday, September 3.
The agency said that the minor allegedly conspired with a 14-year-old boy who was found to be not criminally liable.
“The murder case is pending in court,” it said.
In the press briefing, Justice Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato disclosed that Tacloban prosecutors ordered the filing of additional charges against the 15-year-old student:

items: Four counts of frustrated murder, with recommended bail of P72,000 for each count
Six counts of attempted murder, with recommended bail of P36,000 for each count

blocks.text: According to Dato, Tacloban prosecutors found that the 15 year old “acted with discernment” and in “conspiracy with a second minor.”

“If the CICL (child in conflict with the law) has shown his ability to distinguish between right and wrong and still proceeded to commit the wrong, his acts prior, during, and after the incident would form the context within which to determine discernment,” Dato explained without mentioning specifics of the case.

blocks.caption: You are mistaken if you think minors tagged in crimes are not liable under the law

blocks.text: He said that while the local social welfare and development official initially determines discernment of the CICL, it is not binding on the prosecutors.
“The prosecutors have looked into the entirety of the documentary evidence. I believe some psychological reports have been looked into,” the DOJ official added.
Although the 14-year-old student is exempt from criminal liability, the Department of the Interior and Local Government previously said he would undergo an intervention program.

On August 18, another fatal school shooting incident occurred, this time in Zamboanga City. Two students were killed at Ateneo de Zamboanga University’s junior high school campus, including the perpetrator.
The incidents have sparked discussions of responsible gun ownership, strengthening school safety, and addressing mental health issues among the youth. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Dengue cases in Zamboanga City surge past 2,400
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Dengue cases in Zamboanga City have reached 2,413 from January 1 to August 29, following the addition of 80 new cases recorded during morbidity week 34 from…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Dengue cases in Zamboanga City have reached 2,413 from January 1 to August 29, following the addition of 80 new cases recorded during morbidity week 34 from August 23–29, the Zamboanga City Health Office (CHO) reported.
The death toll stands at 17, though no fatalities were recorded during the latest reporting period.
Patients range in age from four months to 86 years old, with children aged 1 to 10 years old comprising 51 percent (1,220 cases) of the total infections.

CHO data showed that eight barangays registered new cases during the week, including Cawit, which went from zero to two cases, while Guisao, Capisan, Quiniput, Pasilmanta, and Buenavista each reported one case after previously recording none.
The CHO also confirmed case clustering in 60 of the city’s 98 barangays, defined as at least three dengue cases reported in one barangay within four consecutive morbidity weeks.

The top ten barangays with dengue cases for January 1 to August 29 were: Sta. Maria with 138 cases, Calarian with 135, Ayala with 110, Tumaga with 102, Mercedes with 99, Tetuan with 97, Divisoria with 57, Tulungatung with 56, Boalan with 49, and Sta. Catalina with 48.

As the epidemic continues to spread, the city government has intensified search and destroy operations and clean-up drives across barangays to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and reduce transmission risks.

CHO reiterated calls for vigilance, urging households to practice the 5S strategy — search and destroy breeding sites, self-protection, seek early consultation, support fogging/spraying, and sustain hydration — to curb the rising number of infections. /mr

articles.title: ‘Bantay Kalikasan’ drive leads to 490 arrests in Western Visayas
articles.summary: LOILO CITY — Authorities arrested nearly 500 individuals and confiscated over P27.3 million worth of illegal catch, timber, and equipment during a month-long environmental crackdown across Western…

blocks.text: LOILO CITY — Authorities arrested nearly 500 individuals and confiscated over P27.3 million worth of illegal catch, timber, and equipment during a month-long environmental crackdown across Western Visayas in August, the Police Regional Office 6 (PRO6) reported.

According to the consolidated accomplishment report released by PRO6, a total of 490 individuals were taken into custody following 635 operations conducted from August 1 to 31, under the intensified “PRO6 Bantay Kalikasan” campaign.
Maritime crackdown
In the campaign against illegal fishing, regional law enforcers conducted 202 operations, resulting in the arrest of 315 individuals.

Police seized an estimated P550,150 worth of illegally caught fish, alongside various fishing gear, paraphernalia, and motorized boats valued at P25,602,350. Total marine-related seizures reached P26,152,500.

The Antique Police Provincial Office (PPO) spearheaded the drive in terms of operations, conducting 85 anti-illegal fishing raids that led to 87 arrests. Meanwhile, the Iloilo Police Provincial Office (IPPO) registered the highest number of apprehensions, detaining 141 individuals from across 73 operations.
Illegal logging
In forestry protection efforts, police launched 433 anti-illegal logging operations, leading to the arrest of 175 individuals.
Operations led to the recovery of forest products, including illegally harvested lumber, with an estimated value of P1,176,779.45.
Antique PPO led the anti-logging campaign with 134 operations and 124 arrests, followed closely by Aklan PPO, which recorded 122 operations and 45 arrests.
Overall, PRO6 operations against illegal fishing and logging yielded total seizures and recoveries valued at P27,329,279.45 for the month of August.

Police Brigadier General Randulf T. Tuaño, PRO6 director, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to strictly enforcing environmental laws to safeguard the region’s marine habitats, forests, and biodiversity.

“Protecting our environment is an integral part of maintaining safety and order in our communities. We will continuously intensify our operations against illegal fishing, illegal logging, and other destructive activities,” Tuaño said.
PRO6 also appealed to the public for continued cooperation, encouraging residents to promptly report any illegal or suspicious environmental activities to the nearest police station. /mr

articles.title: DepEd leads nationwide school safety drill for emergency readiness
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) spearheaded the National Simultaneous School Safety Drill on Thursday to strengthen the emergency preparedness of public and private schools.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) spearheaded the National Simultaneous School Safety Drill on Thursday to strengthen the emergency preparedness of public and private schools.

The drill aims to enhance multi-agency coordination during active threat scenarios with localized school contingency plans to ensure the safety and psychosocial well-being of students, teachers, and other school personnel.

According to a DepEd statement, the safety drill at Carlos F. Gonzales High School in Bulacan was attended by Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and DepEd officials, led by Undersecretary for Governance and Operations Malcolm Garma.

In a message, which was read on his behalf, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said: “We want our schools to be places where a learner’s biggest concern is an upcoming exam, a missed assignment, or simply getting through another busy day at school, not whether they are safe inside their own classroom.”

“This drill is not about dwelling on frightening situations. It is about making sure that when an emergency happens, our school community knows how to respond. The purpose of a drill is not to look perfect. It is to help us become better prepared,” added Angara.
Angara also thanked teachers for their steadfast commitment to protecting students during any emergency.
Updated drill guidelines

DepEd conducted the drill after extensive consultations with medical and mental health experts, including the Philippine Psychiatric Association, the Philippine Society for Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, and the Philippine Pediatric Society.

The result is updated drill guidelines to align with trauma-informed, child-centered standards under a strict “Do No Harm” directive, which strictly prohibits “hyper-realistic elements, active aggressor role-playing, and graphic threat simulations.”

“Instead, drills are triggered by a distinct early warning alarm, separate from standard fire or earthquake signals, to build procedural muscle memory without creating distress,” the DepEd statement said.

At Carlos F. Gonzales High School, the drill began with an emergency alert via a public address system and calls to the 911 emergency hotline and local police, prompting teachers and students to execute protective actions inside classrooms.
Then police officers arrived — operating under strict safety protocols, with firearms concealed — and cleared response teams to conduct first aid while the school started reunification procedures.

Observers from various agencies were present, including representatives from the Department of the Interior and Local Government, the Philippine National Police, and Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices. They evaluated the simulation to identify operational gaps and refine localized contingency plans.
School Contingency Plan

To ensure campus readiness, DepEd is also doing a nationwide rollout of the new School Contingency Plan integrating active threat responses, such as lockout, lockdown, evacuation, and reunification procedures, into the school’s existing disaster management frameworks.
Schools are mandated to implement physical site hardening, capacity-building, and localized preparations in coordination with local government and law enforcement authorities.
Site hardening measures include the following:

items: single-entry points for visitors
secure perimeter gates
routine inspections of perimeter fencing
internal classroom locking or barricading mechanisms

blocks.text: In the event of a threat, the School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (SDRRM) Committee automatically reconstitutes into an Incident Management Team (IMT). School personnel and students are given orientations and drills in localized, age-appropriate protective actions.

Comprehensive response and reunification guidelines detail strict behavioral compliance during police tactical interventions, multi-agency emergency dispatch, integrated Emergency Medical Services triage, and secure family reunification procedures.

Post-incident protocols call for immediate Psychological First Aid (PFA) and structured learning continuity under DepEd’s 4H (Hinto, Hinga, Hinay, Hayo) Framework for a safe, phased recovery after any active threat has been resolved. /atm

articles.title: Cops arrest 1,000 suspects, seize P19M in contraband in Eastern Visayas
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — The Police Regional Office 8 (PRO-8) intensified its campaign against criminality and other law violations across Eastern Visayas in August, arresting 1,145 violators and…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — The Police Regional Office 8 (PRO-8) intensified its campaign against criminality and other law violations across Eastern Visayas in August, arresting 1,145 violators and confiscating contraband and other illegal items valued at P18.96 million in 1,012 law enforcement operations.

The PRO-8 sustained its focused and intelligence-driven operations against illegal drugs, insurgency, wanted persons, smuggling, illegal fishing, illegal logging, loose firearms and explosives, and illegal gambling.

The campaign against illegal drugs remained among PRO-8’s top priorities. A total of 105 anti-drug operations were conducted, resulting in the arrest of 126 drug personalities and the seizure of 1,145.80 grams of shabu with an estimated street value of P7.79 million.

PRO-8 also continued its anti-insurgency efforts, resulting in the surrender of 19 New People’s Army members and the arrest of two others. The operations also led to the recovery of nine firearms and two explosives, contributing to government efforts to weaken the armed group’s presence and activities in the region.

Meanwhile, intensified manhunt operations led to the arrest of 445 wanted persons, including 74 most wanted persons, as PRO-8 continued its efforts to locate and apprehend individuals with standing warrants of arrest.

Anti-smuggling operations likewise yielded significant results. Four operations targeting cigarette smuggling resulted in the confiscation of five packs and 14 reams of smuggled cigarettes valued at P10,450.00. In separate anti-petroleum smuggling operations, authorities arrested five individuals and seized 108 containers holding 140 liters of petroleum products worth P174,680.00.

In support of environmental protection and the enforcement of fisheries laws, PRO-8 conducted anti-illegal fishing operations that resulted in the apprehension of 292 violators. Authorities also confiscated fishing paraphernalia valued at P10.15 million along with fish catch worth P130,735.00.
Anti-illegal logging operations, meanwhile, led to the arrest of 21 individuals and the seizure of 11,495.10 board feet of illegally sourced lumber with an estimated value of P682,266.00.
PRO-8 also intensified its campaign against loose firearms and explosives through 203 operations, resulting in the confiscation, surrender, and recovery of 191 firearms and two explosives.

The police regional office likewise sustained its crackdown on illegal gambling. A total of 71 operations were conducted, leading to the arrest of 180 individuals and the confiscation of P27,771 in bet money.
B/Gen. Jason Capoy, police regional director, commended the operating units for their dedication and commitment to PRO-8’s intensified law enforcement campaign.

“These accomplishments reflect the hard work, professionalism, and teamwork of our personnel in fulfilling our duty to protect the people of Eastern Visayas. We will continue to strengthen our law enforcement operations through focused and intelligence-driven efforts to ensure that those who violate the law are held accountable. Together, we will continue to maintain peace, order, and public safety throughout the region,” he said in a statement. /mr

articles.title: Amid harsh monsoon, Baguio celebrates 81st year of Yamashita surrender
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — Ignoring the harsh monsoon weather, the sons and daughters of World War II veterans celebrated the 81st year since Imperial Japanese Army Gen. Tomoyuki Yamashita formally…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — Ignoring the harsh monsoon weather, the sons and daughters of World War II veterans celebrated the 81st year since Imperial Japanese Army Gen. Tomoyuki Yamashita formally surrendered at Camp John Hay, ending the Pacific leg of the global war in September 3, 1945.

Baguio Rep. Mauricio Domogan said the war was a terrible experience for Filipinos who suffered the brutality of Japanese military occupation for four years, particularly in Baguio which became Yamashita’s last stronghold when Allied Forces began liberating towns that was invaded.
Recently dubbed as “Victory Day,” September 3 is memorialized for Yamashita signing Japan’s surrender documents in the presence ofAmerican Generals Arthur Percival and Jonathan Wainwright.

Historians recently pointed out that Camp John Hay was also where the Pacific War began, when it was attacked by Japanese fighters on December 8,1941 shortly after Japan’s attack at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941 – making Baguio pivotal to the Pacific War.

The battles did not end with Yamashita’s surrender after he was cornered by indigenous Filipino guerrillas and Allied soldiers in Ifugao’s Kiangan town on September 2, because “mopping operations” took days here and in the Visayas, said Miguel Villa-real, Philippine Veterans Bank First Vice President for Marketing and Communications, and a veteran’s son.

The 66th Infantry Regiment, composed of Igorot soldiers and guerrillas who served as the Resistance in this part of the country, proved instrumental in freeing Baguio and other Cordilleran towns from the Japanese, Domogan said.

Before the celebration at Baguio’s Veterans Park in front of Burnham Park, the group unveiled a repainted monument and a marker at Naguilian Road which represents one of the three gateways opened by the Igorot Infantry Regiment and American soldiers as they battled to liberate the summer capital.

Domogan said the end of the Pacific War and the end of World War II as a whole led “to the (global) realization of democratic principles, and affirmation of human rights and the dignity and self respect among nations which we have been aspiring for after centuries of colonial domination.”
Villa-real and Domogan again urged Malacañang and Congress to make Victory Day a national non-working holiday. “September 3 is not just about Baguio. It is about the whole nation,” the lawmaker said.

articles.title: Rappler Live Jam: The cast of ‘Muli: An OPM Musical’
articles.summary: Set across the '90s and early 2000s, the musical 'Muli' moves through different eras and sounds of OPM

blocks.text: LIVE

blocks.caption: Rappler Live Jam: The cast of ‘Muli: An OPM Musical’

blocks.text: Set across the '90s and early 2000s, the musical 'Muli' moves through different eras and sounds of OPM

MANILA, Philippines – Muli: An OPM Musical brings its original music to Rappler Live Jam on Thursday, September 3, giving audiences a preview of the songs behind its story of missed chances, old dreams, and the prospect of starting anew.

The musical follows Anita, a 42-year-old housewife who finds herself looking back on the past two decades and reflecting on the possibilities of the different paths she might have taken. Her daughter Kath encourages her to look beyond the life she has built around motherhood and rediscover the dreams she once had for herself.

Set across the ’90s and early 2000s, the musical moves through different eras and sounds of OPM, with 11 original songs written and produced by singer-songwriter Nica del Rosario and musical director and composer Matthew Chang alongside talents from FlipMusic, the team behind BINI favorites “Pantropiko,” “Salamin, Salamin,” and “Karera,” as well as the Sarah Geronimo hit “Tala.”

The musical stars Gawad Urian award-winning actress Kakki Teodoro as Anita and OPM artist Janine Teñoso as her daughter Kath, with ensemble cast members Vien King, Marvin Ong, Justine Peña, Marynor Mademesila, and Baus Rufo.
Muli also marks Janine’s theater stage debut after establishing herself through OPM and Filipino OST hits.
Showdates run from September 11-27 at the Globe Auditorium, Maybank Performing Arts Theater at the BGC Arts Center in Taguig City.
Catch the cast of Muli: An OPM Musical on Rappler Live Jam on Thursday, September 3, at 8 pm, by bookmarking this page or heading to Rappler’s YouTube! – Belle Calica/Rappler.com

articles.title: Apocalypse prep or pure pragmatism: what is behind Peter Thiel’s move to Argentina?
articles.summary:
Relocation coincides with proposed laws that opponents say would entrench power of US tech billionaires in country

Dozens of protesters converged on Peter Thiel’s mansion in Buenos Aires…

blocks.text: Dozens of protesters converged on Peter Thiel’s mansion in Buenos Aires this week after a congressional session raised questions about the billionaire’s presence in the country.

In white masks, they held signs saying “Peter Thief” and “No to the Peter Thiel law” in front of the wrought-iron gates of the $12m (£8.9m) residence, which Thiel bought in April as he moved his family to Argentina.

There is broad unease at the tech magnate’s presence in the country. His move has been characterised as part of a plan to hedge against world war three: Argentina, agriculturally rich and deep in the southern hemisphere, might just be the ideal place for a tech billionaire to wait out the apocalypse.
But recent developments in the country suggest Thiel could have more pragmatic considerations.

blocks.caption: Protesters marched to the gates of the $12m residence Peter Thiel bought when he moved his family to Argentina in April.  Photograph: Tomás Cuesta/Reuters

blocks.text: Last week, Argentina’s chamber of deputies held a six-hour debate on a set of sweeping regulatory changes put forward by Javier Milei’s rightwing government shortly after Thiel moved to Buenos Aires. They invited Thiel, Milei and an official linked to Argentina’s intelligence services to answer questions.
“None of them answered, and none of them came to the meeting,” said Juan Marino, a member of the chamber of deputies and the leader of the Piquetero party.

Marino said the new laws amounted to a “technofascist legislative package” aimed at entrenching the power of US tech billionaires in the country. Thiel has not publicly advocated for them, but Marino and others have said that their timing was suggestive.

The meeting in the chamber of deputies came after Argentinian deputies from several parties made public requests to the government for information about Thiel, his meetings and his businesses. None have been answered.

blocks.caption: Peter Thiel held closed-door meetings with Javier Milei and key presidential advisers in the months after he moved to Argentina. Photograph: Gage Skidmore/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: One of the laws, the “super RIGI”, would put in place an investment regime offering foreign companies a minimal tax rate and a 30-year guarantee against regulatory change. It specifically names AI datacentres among investments it hopes to attract.

Another, which failed, aimed to eliminate most of the restrictions around foreigners buying land in Argentina. A final decree would require some civilian government departments to share vast amounts of personal data on Argentinian citizens with the state intelligence services.

There is no evidence that Thiel has advocated for these laws directly. But in the months after he moved to Buenos Aires, he held closed-door meetings with Milei and key presidential advisers. It is uncommon for a foreign investor to have this degree of access.
In the regulatory package, Marino and others see the footprint of Thiel’s larger techno-libertarian interests.

The decree that gives vast amounts of Argentinians’ personal data to state intelligence services comes as Argentinian deputies have asked increasingly pointed questions about whether Palantir, the company Thiel co-founded, has undisclosed contracts with the state, which have gone unanswered.

blocks.caption: One of the proposed laws protesters oppose would offer foreign companies a minimal tax rate and a 30-year guarantee against regulatory change.  Photograph: Tomás Cuesta/Reuters

blocks.text: The land law, said Marino, could have paved the way for semi-autonomous “startup cities” – such as the controversial Próspera development in Honduras – that Thiel has advocated as a way for libertarians to carve out zones outside state control.

“Argentina is kind of a laboratory,” said Cecilia Nicolini, who represents Argentina at the Mercosur regional parliament. US tech billionaires, she said, “are using Argentina as a laboratory, because they have a person in power, Milei, who is even more crazy than they are”.
Over the summer Milei wrote an article in the Financial Times advocating the creation of “non-human corporations” – “entities operated by AI agents or robots”.

It parallels a vision put forward by OpenAI’s chief executive, Sam Altman, who predicted in 2024 that the world could soon be run by AI-owned companies. It also raises dark, thorny questions about the legal liabilities of those entities.
Nicolini said: “It’s not just that [Thiel] chose Argentina in terms of, it’s a secure place to live in a world that is facing a number of wars, etcetera.
“But really, behind it, I think there is a clear plan. And it is related to reforms that Milei is trying to pass, with some success in some cases, and in others, backlash.”
Thiel was approached for comment.

articles.title: Malaysia's middle path between China and US faces new tests
articles.summary: The prime minister's comments on Taiwan and US-backed military facilities near Sabah have revived questions over Malaysia's non-aligned foreign policy.

image.caption: US President Trump visited Malaysia during a tour of Asia last year [FILE: October 26, 2025]Image: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP

blocks.text: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has spent much of his time in office insisting that Kuala Lumpur will not be forced to choose between the United States and China.
But two sets of comments last month have raised questions about how sustainable that position is as rivalry between the two superpowers increasingly spills into Southeast Asia.
"I see Taiwan as part of China, period," he said in an interview with news outlet Al Jazeera that aired on August 16.

Beijing considers democratically governed Taiwan part of its territory. While Chinese leaders say they favor "peaceful reunification," they have never ruled out using force to bring the island under Beijing's control.
More controversially, Anwar appeared to accept Beijing's argument that force could be necessary.
"If one province decides to break away. Do we use force? I think I will, [to] protect the sanctity and unity of the nation," he said.
China's gray zone warfare in the Pacific
Regional concerns

The comments drew an enthusiastic response from Beijing, while Taiwan's Foreign Ministry accused Anwar of effectively legitimizing the use of force against the islandand warned that his "one-sided support for China could negatively impact Taiwanese businesses' confidence in investing in Malaysia," including in the country's strategically important semiconductor sector.

Two days after his comments on Taiwan aired, Anwar argued that Malaysiashould strengthen its defenses in Sabah, citing the expansion of US-backed military facilities on the nearby Philippine island of Balabac.
The Philippines is upgrading facilities on Balabac, roughly 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the Malaysian islands of Banggi and Balambangan.

Balabac was one of four additional locations added in 2023 to the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement, which allows US forces to access designated Philippine military facilities, construct infrastructure and pre-position equipment.
Taken together, Anwar's comments raised concerns that Malaysia is growing warmer towards Beijing while becoming more suspicious of Washington's military footprint in the region.
A fundamental realignment?

Kuala Lumpur has also been one of the region's strongest critics of Israel's actions in Gaza. Anwar has repeatedly accused the United States and European governments of hypocrisy and double standards for championing democracy and international law while failing, in his view, to hold Israel sufficiently accountable.
But Malaysia experts warn against interpreting Anwar's rhetoric as evidence of a fundamental strategic realignment.
"Malaysia still maintains very good relations with the US and other Western countries," Ngeow Chow Bing, director of the Institute of China Studies at Universiti Malaya, told DW.
Those ties may sometimes be less visible than Anwar's increasingly warm public rhetoric towards Beijing, Bing said, but the underlying relationship remains strong.

"It is certainly true that the space for maintaining its traditional balancing act between China and the US is narrower than before, but that space remains, and Malaysia will continue to operate within it," Bing added.
Philippine island on edge amid fear of China-Taiwan conflict
A shift in tone, not strategy

Anwar's comments about the Philippine military build-up are much more about an ongoing territorial dispute between Kuala Lumpur and Manila, Chee Meng Tan, assistant professor at the University of Nottingham Malaysia, told DW.

The Philippines maintains a territorial claim over Sabah, which became part of Malaysia when the federation was formed in 1963. Malaysia rejects the claim and regards its sovereignty over the state as indisputable.
Those tensions resurface regularly, and last month Kuala Lumpur lodged a fresh objection with the United Nations over a Philippine submission about its continental shelf.
"A neighbor that claims part of your territory is building a military base 20 minutes offshore — any government would react," said Tan.
Anwar called for the strengthening of Malaysia's own defenses, not for Chinese help, "and he went out of his way to say relations with Manila remain good," Tan added.

Anwar also sought to lower the temperature over Taiwan after his initial comments. Speaking to Malaysian media after the event, he stressed that Kuala Lumpur wanted a peaceful resolution to cross-Strait tensions and insisted that Malaysia's position had not changed.
Malaysia has formally followed a "One China" policy since establishing diplomatic relations with Beijing in 1974.

Chinese state media quickly interpreted Anwar's remarks through Beijing's preferred terminology, with Xinhua reporting that the Malaysian leader had "reaffirmed the one-China principle," something Malaysian analysts said isn't true.

Malaysia has not abandoned its traditional position, but Anwar's rhetoric "has sometimes been more accommodating towards Beijing than necessary," Khoo Ying Hooi, associate professor of international relations at Universiti Malaya, told DW.
"That can create the perception of a tilt even when Malaysia's wider strategic behavior remains more hedged and pragmatic," she added.
Less room to hedge
The prime minister faces mounting political pressure after his Pakatan Harapan coalition suffered three consecutive setbacks in state elections.
The defeats have intensified tensions within Anwar's broad governing alliance and speculation that he could call a snap general election.
Yet beyond Anwar's rhetoric and domestic political calculations lies a more structural problem for Malaysia.

Its longstanding strategy of hedging between the United States and China is becoming more difficult as Beijing's economic and military weight grows and Washington takes an increasingly transactional approach to foreign relations.
How much leverage does the US have over its adversaries?
"Malaysia is not abandoning its traditional balancing strategy, but the space for ambiguity is narrowing," said Hooi

Anwar is expected to visit China in late September, his first trip there in more than a year. He is reportedly due to attend the Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou and hold talks with Chinese Premier Li Qiang as Kuala Lumpur seeks to deepen economic ties with its largest trading partner.
But closer relations with Beijing do not remove Malaysia's dependence on Western markets, investment and technology, or its own differences with China.
Despite warm political ties, Kuala Lumpur continues to reject Chinese maritime claims in the South China Sea that overlap with waters Malaysia considers its own.

In February, Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan reiterated that Malaysia would not recognize Chinese claims that conflict with its maritime boundaries in the South China Sea, while Anwar has recently insisted that Malaysian oil and gas exploration will continue in the waters despite objections from Beijing.
For Tan, Malaysia's ability to continue balancing the two powers ultimately depends less on Anwar's rhetoric than on Malaysia remaining valuable to both.
"China wants friendly neighbors to keep trading with, and America needs Malaysian factories, where a big share of the world's chips is tested and packaged," said Tan.
"Neither gains from pushing Malaysia toward the other."

articles.title: Iran bets on shadow networks to evade US sanctions
articles.summary: To circumvent US sanctions, Iran has spent decades building a complex network of businesspeople and companies. A billionaire once sentenced to death is now back at its center.

image.caption: Iran is seeking new ways to bypass increasingly stringent US sanctions [FILE: February 23, 2016]Image: Ahmad Halabisaz/Xinhua/IMAGO

blocks.text: With its toughest sanctions yet, the administration of US President Donald Trump is seeking to force Iran's leadership into submission.
The measures, dubbed "economic D-Day" sanctions, are intended to achieve what military pressure since February has failed to accomplish.

In addition to targeting Iran's key sources of revenue and trade, including oil, banking, gold, shipping, aviation and certain technology sectors, US authorities are increasingly focusing on cryptocurrencies.

Digital currencies such as bitcoin, which operate outside the traditional banking system and dollar-based financial networks, are being used by Iran for money transfers, trade transactions and, increasingly, oil-related business.
An opaque network to help Tehran bypass sanctions
Iran also appears to be exploring cryptocurrencies as a way to secure oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
According to the Fars News Agency, which is close to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, the idea was proposed by Babak Zanjani.
The 53-year-old billionaire was released from prison last year and remains one of the most prominent figures in a network that has grown over decades and helped Iran navigate international sanctions.

blocks.caption: In 2016, Zanjani became entangled in Iran's internal power struggles and was sentenced to deathImage: Tasnim News/AFP

blocks.text: Individuals within these networks enjoy support and protection from influential figures inside the Islamic Republic. In return, they are believed to share part of their profits with powerful patrons within the system.

"Among these people, Zanjani belongs to an economic elite with innovative ideas and has repeatedly demonstrated his capabilities in the past," said Behzad Ahmadinia, an Iran-born journalist based in Cyprus who specializes in the oil and energy sector.
"It appears that the regime has decided to overcome internal rivalries and rely on professionals and experts who can work more efficiently than others and take over key positions."
Selling oil barrels on the black market

Iran can draw on decades of experience in operating under sanctions. The system extends far beyond individual businessmen and includes a vast network of companies, financial channels and personal connections.

Corruption and a lack of transparency are widely regarded as structural problems within Iran's political and economic system. Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 gave Iran a score of 23 out of 100 and ranked it 153rd out of 182 countries, indicating a very high perceived level of public-sector corruption.
Zanjani reportedly controlled a business empire of around 60 companies, including entities in Malaysia, Tajikistan, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates.

Many of these firms were later sanctioned by the United States. Through this network, Zanjani began selling billions of barrels of Iranian oil on the black market during the presidency of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, while also importing a wide range of goods, including aircraft, into Iran.
Is Iran set to become an economic outcast?
In 2016, however, he became entangled in Iran's internal power struggles. Authorities accused him of failing to return around $2.6 billion (€2.24 billion) in oil revenues to the Iranian state.

After a highly publicized trial in one of the country's biggest corruption cases, he was sentenced to death. For years, he disputed claims over the missing funds and negotiated with Iranian authorities.
US gains insight into sanctions-evasion routes

A key link in this network was Turkish-Iranian businessman Reza Zarrab. He was arrested in the United States in 2016 while on vacation and accused of money laundering and violating US sanctions on Iran.
Zarrab had built an extensive network in Turkey and possessed detailed knowledge of the financial and trading mechanisms Iran used to bypass sanctions.

Cases such as his gave US authorities valuable insight into how Iranian sanctions-evasion networks operate, allowing Washington to target them more effectively. Zarrab later cooperated with US investigators and was released from custody. According to reports, he now lives in the United States under a new identity.
"People like Zarrab or Zanjani are cultivated within the system and maintain connections to different centers of power," France-based economist Jamshid Assadi told DW.
Can the US 'asphyxiate' Iran without taking on China?

According to reports, Zanjani's rise began some 30 years ago during his military service, when he worked as a driver for the governor of Iran's central bank. The position is said to have opened doors to influential circles and provided him with key business contacts. How many billions of dollars flowed through his network and companies, and how much he personally earned from those activities, remains unclear.

In February 2024, Iranian media reported that assets linked to Zanjani had been repatriated from abroad. His wealth, they said, had grown beyond the value of his outstanding liabilities. In 2025, he was released from prison and quickly returned to the business world. Through one of his companies, he signed a multibillion-dollar contract with Iran's state railway operator.

At the same time, Zanjani has sought to reinvent himself. In an open letter to US business magnate Elon Musk, he offered his company as a bridge for economic cooperation between Iran and the United States. He now presents himself as an entrepreneur, mediator and advocate of dialogue.

After the United States placed Zanjani back on its sanctions list in January 2026, Washington expanded its measures in July to target a broader network of companies and business associates linked to him.

Just one day before the new sanctions were announced, Zanjani opened a café and pastry shop in western Tehran and attended a celebratory launch event. The business was shut down by authorities the following day.
Allies to adversaries: US-Iran relations over the decades
Can the US cripple Iran's shadow networks?
The key question, however, is whether the latest US measures can truly reach the networks underpinning Iran's shadow economy.

According to Jamshid Assadi, many of the traditional sanctions-evasion routes are now well known and increasingly difficult for Tehran to use. The United States has warned numerous countries that their companies, banks and private-sector actors could face penalties if they help Iran bypass restrictions.

At the same time, Iran has spent decades adapting to economic pressure and finding new ways around it. Whether Washington's latest sanctions will significantly weaken those networks remains uncertain. But the return of Babak Zanjani suggests that Tehran is once again turning to the businessmen who helped it weather previous periods of economic isolation.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan again denies Jinggoy Estrada’s bid for bail
articles.summary: Estrada may still seek temporary liberty through a formal bail petition

blocks.text: BJMP. Senator Jinggoy Estrada arrives at the Sandiganbayan graft court in Quezon City on June 2, 2026, for the arraignment of his graft case.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Estrada may still seek temporary liberty through a formal bail petition
MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan upheld its resolution to deny Senator Jinggoy Estrada’s request for bail in his flood control-related case.
In a resolution dated Thursday, September 3, the court’s 5th Division junked Estrada’s motion for reconsideration, which appealed the court’s earlier resolution to deny the bail request.

“Accordingly, the court finds no cogent reason to disturb its earlier ruling. Until a hearing determines that the evidence of guilt is not strong, the court has no basis to set a bail amount. Consequently, the motion is denied,” the resolution penned by Associate Justice Gener Gito read.
“Wherefore, premises considered, accused Jose ‘Jinggoy’ Pimentel Ejercito Estrada’s Motion for Reconsideration dated August 3, 2026 is denied for lack of merit,” it added.
Associate Justices Zaldy Trespeses and Maryann Corpus-Mañalac concurred.
Estrada was charged with plunder and graft cases in May due to his alleged involvement in the flood control corruption.

The Sandiganbayan junked Estrada’s request in July because it had no legal basis and was filed prematurely. This denial, however, does not preclude Estrada from filing an actual bail petition before the Sandiganbayan, where the prosecution will try to establish that the evidence of his guilt is strong.

In its recent resolution, the Sandiganbayan did not give weight to Estrada’s claim that he is not a flight risk, explaining that “such circumstance does not authorize the court to dispense with the requisite bail proceedings and immediately fix bail.”
Estrada also used the Enrile doctrine, where the court granted former senator Juan Ponce Enrile’s request for bail due to humanitarian concerns.

“The [Enrile] ruling cannot reasonably be understood as establishing a general rule that an accused charged with an offense punishable by reclusion perpetua may obtain bail without the requisite determination of whether the evidence of guilt is strong merely upon showing that he is not a flight risk, possesses substantial social or political ties, or has previously complied with travel conditions imposed by this court,” it explained.

“The considerations concerning his alleged lack of flight risk do not dispense with the antecedent determination of whether the evidence of guilt is strong. Neither does Enrile, considering the exceptional factual circumstances underlying that ruling, authorize the court to circumvent the procedure regarding discretionary bail under the circumstances of this case,” it added. – Rappler.com

articles.title: New name, old problems? Bulacan water woes continue despite PrimeWater rebrand
articles.summary: Residents of San Jose del Monte, Bulacan cry for help amid continued water service problems despite PrimeWater's acquisition by Crystal Bridges Holding Corp. in December 2025

blocks.text: TAWID-UHAW. Weak water supply comes out of a Tawid-Uhaw PrimeWater station in San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan.
Franz Lopez/Rappler
Residents of San Jose del Monte, Bulacan cry for help amid continued water service problems despite PrimeWater's acquisition by Crystal Bridges Holding Corp. in December 2025

items: Hiraya Water Corp., formerly PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation, continues to face significant water service issues, affecting over 47,000 households in San Jose del Monte City.

Residents have expressed dissatisfaction with the lack of public consultation regarding the transfer of water services to a private concessionaire, leading to ongoing service interruptions and poor water quality.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
A new name did not erase PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation’s longstanding problems.
Despite its rebranding as Hiraya Water Corp., persistent water woes and unfulfilled obligations continued to hound the private concessionaire, with consumers bearing the brunt.

In San Jose del Monte City, Bulacan, Senator Raffy Tulfo — chairperson of the Senate Public Services committee — said over 47,000 households remained reeling from frequent service interruptions, as well as discolored water supply even months after Lucio Co’s Crystal Bridges Holding Corp. acquired PrimeWater in late 2025.

“Nung pumasok ang PrimeWater, ‘yung ganda ng serbisyo ng water district…nawala,” Irene del Rosario, resident and former San Jose del Monte city councilor, told the Senate Public Services Committee during a hearing on the joint venture agreements (JVAs) of water districts and private entities on Thursday, September 3.
(When PrimeWater entered into the picture, the good services of the water district vanished.)

Del Rosario recalled the water district entered into a JVA with PrimeWater in 2018 following an “unsolicited” proposal from the private concessionaire. This was allegedly approved by then newly-appointed members of the board of directors.
“Walang public consultation. Hindi alam ng taumbayan na ang tubig namin ay iliipat na sa isang private concessionaire…[Ngayon], ganun pa rin, as expected,” she said.
(There was no public consultation. We did not know that our water service would be transferred to a private concessionaire. Now, our situation remains the same, as expected.)

Residents of San Jose del Monte have repeatedly called for intervention amid continued poor water service in the area. In March, the city government assumed control of the water service previously managed by PrimeWater. It tapped Metro Pacific Water (MPW) to take over the service as an interim operator two months later.

MPW head of legal Roberto Rey Rodrigo said the company had started rehabilitating the city’s water service assets but admitted that San Jose del Monte had a deficit of about 70 million liters to fulfill its daily water requirement.
“Unfortunately, to take on such a monumental task would require a long-term concessionaire,” Rodrigo added.

On August 23, a crowd consisting of many local residents chanted “Tubig! Tubig! Tubig!” (Water!) in a sports event after learning that Mayor Rita Robes, and her husband, Congressman Arthur Robes, were at the venue.
“Sumigaw sila ng ‘Tubig!’ Kasi wala talaga kaming tubig,” Akbayan Councilor Ronalyn Pordan previously told Rappler. (They shouted “Water!” because we really have no water.)

Senator Raffy Tulfo, chairperson of the Senate panel, flagged Hiraya Water for the persistent water issues in its areas of operation. He also questioned the concessionaire over its corporate records, citing a Securities and Exchange Commission record showing it previously listed “restaurants, parlors, beer houses and snack bars” as its nature of business.
“Nagbago na ang owner ng PrimeWater, pero patuloy pa rin ang reklamo,” said Tulfo. (The ownership of PrimeWater changed but the complaints over their service have not stopped.)

“To be fair, Crystal Bridges did not create PrimeWater’s problems. Pero kapag bumili ka ng kumpanya, hindi lang assets at revenue ang kasama. You inherit the existing contracts, debts and obligations, pending cases, unfinished commitments and consumers na galit na, uhaw pa,” the lawmaker added.

(To be fair, Crystal Bridges did not create PrimeWater’s problems but when you buy out a company, you acquire not only their assets and revenue, but also their existing contracts, debts and obligations, pending cases, unfinished commitments and consumers who are not only angry but also thirsty.)

PrimeWater is a Villar-owned water and wastewater services provider that previously partnered with over 77 water districts in the country. Following the acquisition, Hiraya Water took over the existing JVAs.
Senator Risa Hontiveros, during the legislative inquiry, said she received information that eight water districts are signifying intention to exit the JVA amid the persistent service issues.
Hontiveros asked Hiraya Water whether it intended to file cases or impose penalties on water districts should they pursue the unilateral termination of their contracts.
“Mayroon pong procedure set in place and signed by both parties and was cleared by regulatory bodies. Sana sundin ‘yun,” Hiraya Water president Jose Paulino Santamarina said.
(There’s a procedure set in place and signed by both parties. It was also cleared by regulatory bodies. We’re hoping it will be followed.)

The Public-Private Partnership (PPP) center said Hiraya Water failed to secure the consent of any of the 77 water districts during the acquisition. Sans written consent, the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel (OGCC) said the water districts can move to terminate the JVAs as they were not formally informed of the ownership change.
Apart from the water districts, some private subdivisions including La Poblacion in San Jose del Monte also appealed to Hiraya Water to allow them to exit the water service agreement.

“I-turnover ‘nyo na kami sa water district, ‘yun lang ang solution dun,” said La Poblacion resident Charlie Marciano. (We’re appealing for Hiraya Water to turn over our water service to the city water district. That’s the only solution to our problem.)
Is anyone listening? – Rappler.com

articles.title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies
articles.summary: Millions of people have been exposed to the smog, with more than 12,000 children suffering respiratory issues.
articles.byline: BBC Indonesian, Gavin Butler and Virma Simonette

blocks.text: A blanket of toxic haze is enveloping parts of Indonesia and spreading into Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines, as weeks-long wildfires continue to burn.

Millions of people across large swathes of South East Asia have been exposed to the smog, which in some areas has fuelled "acutely unhealthy" pollution more than 15 times the World Health Organization's recommended level.
Many of the ongoing fires have been burning across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo since mid-July – underpinned by a so-called Super El Niño that is exacerbating drought conditions.
Between July and August, Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of respiratory infections linked to land and forest fires.
More than 12,000 of those cases are of children under the age of five.
Rizma Nur Fatimah, a 19-year-old teaching assistant at a school in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, told the BBC that the smog in her classroom had become so thick "you couldn't even see your own feet".

"Even inside the house, with everything closed, the haze still got in," she said. "We've been living with this since I was born. It's the same every year, so we've almost become resigned to it. But this year is worse."
Misbah, a 23-year-old mother from nearby Pengayuan village, said her three-year-old daughter had developed "a cough, a sore throat and a runny nose" during the haze.
Some 1,300 kilometres away, in the Philippine island province of Palawan, residents reported similar symptoms, including itchy eyes, nose and throat.

"We are now experiencing mild headaches," said Dr Precious Bañas-Melad. "My cousin who isn't allergic to anything started developing allergies. My husband is the first one who had itchy eyes and throat."
Malaysia, meanwhile, has reported rising cases of asthma and conjunctivitis amid worsening air quality nationwide as smoke continues to drift across the border.

Indonesia's forest and peatland fires are not a new phenomenon. Experts say the crisis is rooted in decades of land-use change, dating back to the Suharto era, when vast areas of rainforest and peatland in Kalimantan were opened for logging, plantations and large-scale development projects.

Today, large-scale fires are often associated with the expansion of industrial plantations and other commercial land use. Environmental groups, researchers, and government investigations have repeatedly alleged that some companies use fire as a cheap and effective way to clear vast areas of land.

Some point out that while drought and El Niño conditions help fires spread, the severity of the haze is also linked to human activity. Drained peatlands, industrial timber estates and oil palm plantations can leave landscapes more vulnerable to burning, with fires often recurring in the same areas.

Unlike traditional practices, which are small-scale, community-managed, and closely monitored, fires linked to large-scale land development can be far more difficult to control and can cause environmental and public health impacts on a much larger scale.
What makes Indonesian Borneo's wildfires particularly worrying is that they are burning through one of the world's largest tropical peatland ecosystems.
Under normal conditions, these peatlands serve as gigantic carbon reservoirs. But under abnormal conditions, such as those currently hitting the region, they can become carbon "bombs".

"Peatlands are incredibly effective carbon stores because their waterlogged conditions slow decomposition, allowing carbon to accumulate underground for thousands of years," explains Dr Nisa Novita, a peatland researcher at Indonesian conservation NGO Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara.
"But this also means they can become a 'carbon bomb' when they are drained or burned, because that carbon can be rapidly released into the atmosphere."
Others have warned that as the current Super El Niño continues to escalate over the coming months, the fires could significantly worsen.
Last year, without El Niño, forest fires in Indonesia torched a 359,000-hectare area, says Professor Bambang Hero Saharjo, a forest fire forensics expert from Institut Pertanian Bogor University.

Citing research reports, Prof Bambang told the BBC that this year's El Niño could burn an area as large as 11 million hectares – putting it on par with one of Indonesia's worst wildfire seasons, which happened from 1997 to 1998.
Earlier this week, Indonesia's forestry minister Raja Juli Antoni told reporters that the battle to extinguish the current wildfires was entering a critical phase.
"Our problems are not over. September is the peak of El Niño," he said earlier this week. "September is the main fight for us."

articles.title: Ombudsman sacks BFP chief, files graft charges over P485M ambulance purchase
articles.summary: The Ombudsman has dismissed Bureau of Fire Protection Director Jesus Fernandez after he was found guilty in an administrative case involving cash deliveries worth P14.7 million in 2024 and 2025 from…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 7:33pm

The Ombudsman has dismissed Bureau of Fire Protection Director Jesus Fernandez after he was found guilty in an administrative case involving cash deliveries worth P14.7 million in 2024 and 2025 from the supplier of ambulances worth P485 million.
The office also filed graft and bribery charges against Fernandez and the private contractor before the Sandiganbayan.
The Ombudsman investigation showed that Fernandez, who was then the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) chairperson, allegedly received a total of P14.752 million from the contractor.
The cash deliveries included P10,752,000 on November 21, 2024, and P4 million on September 25, 2025.

The Ombudsman found Fernandez guilty of conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service and grave misconduct, which carries the penalty of dismissal from the service, including cancellation of eligibility, forfeiture of retirement benefits, and perpetual disqualification from reemployment in government service.

Regarding the criminal case, "the Ombudsman found prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction to charge Fernandez with two counts of indirect bribery and two counts of violation of Section 3(b) of Republic Act No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act."

The charges stemmed from a complaint filed by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) following a fact-finding investigation by Task Force BFP Accountability into the procurement of 132 units of Type 1 Basic Life Support ambulances.
The contract for the project was awarded to Toyota Mabolo, which entered into a joint venture with Autozone Prime Distributors, Inc. for the project.

“He (Ferrnandez) is not merely an officer of the BFP. He is the fire chief of the agency. He was the BAC chairman when he received the SOP on 21 November 2024 and the head of the procuring entity when he received the second SOP on 25 September 2025,” the Ombudsman said.

“Receiving any gift, compensation, promise, or consideration from any individual in relation to his position gives the appearance of impropriety, which does not only bring doubt to his credibility but significantly tarnishes the credibility of the agency that he leads, in this case, especially in the process of procurement,” the Ombudsman added.

Likewise, the Ombudsman also charged Rosaverna Palairon Sangga, the designated representative of the joint venture between Toyota Mabolo and Autozone Prime Distributors, Inc., with two counts of Corruption of Public Officials under Article 212 of the Revised Penal Code. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: India news: Jaishankar offers help to end war in Ukraine
articles.summary: Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar says India is prepared to assist efforts to end the war in Ukraine, as the foreign minister visits Kyiv. DW has more.

image.caption: Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar met his Ukrainian counterpart Andriiy Sybiha in KyivImage: Efrem Lukatsky/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: September 3, 2026
India ready to help end Ukraine war, Jaishankar says during Kyiv visit
India is ready to help end the war in Ukraine, Indian Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar said as he arrived in the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, on Thursday.
"If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there," Jaishankar said as he addressed the media alongside Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.
Sybiha welcomed Jaishankar for what he described as the "first-ever dedicated bilateral visit" of an Indian foreign minister to Ukraine.

"India is a global power and we welcome Prime Minister Modi's call to move from an endless war towards an end to the war. Ukraine stands ready for diplomacy," Sybiha wrote on X, referring to comments the Indian leader made during a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan earlier in the week.

Jaishankar's trip to Ukraine comes more than a week after he attended the 27th session of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation in Moscow with his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov.
The Indian foreign minister also met Putin during the Russia visit.
Since the start of Russia's war in Ukraine, New Delhi has been under pressure from Kyiv's Western partners over its cooperation with Moscow, India's decades-long ally.

"This historic moment takes place amid escalating Russian attacks against our cities, port infrastructure, and civil shipping. Our capital is constantly under attack and I appreciate my colleague's brave visit," Sybiha said as he talked about Jaishankar's Kyiv visit.
The Ukrainian minister added that he and Jaishankar discussed the need to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea, global food security, and bilateral cooperation.
"From infrastructure and pharmaceutical sector to technological innovation and digitalisation, we are ready to realise our full potential," Sybiha said.

articles.title: PCG must map assets to boost emergency response ops – Zubiri
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) must start mapping its programs and assets to boost emergency response operations, especially in relation to tourism, Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) must start mapping its programs and assets to boost emergency response operations, especially in relation to tourism, Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri said Thursday.
Zubiri made the pronouncement as the country moves to advance the ratification and implementation of the International Convention on Maritime Search and Rescue, or the SAR convention.

“Given this agreement and the obligations attached to it, I believe you should now prepare your programs and plans—not only at the regional level, but also by organizing your assets, such as air and sea vessel, to ensure a rapid response,” said Zubiri during a Senate foreign relations panel hearing.
According to the senator, having the PCG map its programs will be pivotal due to agency’s current lack of air assets.

“Tourism is the lowest-lying fruit of this country in terms of income, but the Philippines seems to have a reputation that it’s not a safe place to visit—not in peace and order, but in all other things,” he observed.
“Hospitals are far away. There are no air taxis or air ambulances,” Zubiri identified.
“Perhaps once we ratify this, providing these services should become one of our obligations, not just for Filipinos, but for tourists as well,” he added.

Zubiri also cited Senate Bill No. 2971, or the “Sandy’s Bill” and Child Tourist Safety Act, saying that, alongside the measure, basic first-aid awareness and an action plan will become mandatory in tourism facilities.

PCG incumbent commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gaval, for his part, said the ratification of the SAR will bring more cruise ships in the country, thereby increasing the demand for search and rescue services.
“We shall develop better SAR capabilities, because of the positive consequence of this,” said Gaval.
He also said that tourism emergency response is included in the PCG’s Maritime Rescue Coordinating Center Concept, which serves as the coordinating hub for rescue efforts. /apl
