blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY — The Environmental Management Bureau in the Negros Island Region (EMB-NIR) warned that air quality in Bacolod City and other localities in Negros Occidental was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups,” as of noon on Thursday, Sept. 3.
Due to the reduced air quality, the EMB advised individuals with respiratory conditions, such as asthma, to limit outdoor exposure.
Meanwhile, air quality levels in La Carlota City and Canlaon City were reported as fair during the same period.
The advisory reflects a slight improvement from earlier in the day, as 8 a.m. readings recorded significantly worse conditions across the region.

At that time, air quality was rated as “very unhealthy” in Bacolod City, “acutely unhealthy” in La Castellana, and “unhealthy for sensitive groups” in La Carlota City, while Canlaon City remained fair.
Authorities say these situations may have links to smoke and transboundary haze from the ongoing forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia. /apl

articles.title: South Cotabato braces for El Niño occurrence
articles.summary: KORONADAL CITY — South Cotabato has stepped up preparations for a possible strong El Niño event, with disaster officials keeping funds, water facilities and relief supplies ready as the prolonged…

blocks.text: KORONADAL CITY — South Cotabato has stepped up preparations for a possible strong El Niño event, with disaster officials keeping funds, water facilities and relief supplies ready as the prolonged heat and dry conditions threaten farms, livestock and public health.

Rolly Doane Aquino, Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) chief, said the province remains under an El Niño Alert based on information from the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa).
Aquino said South Cotabato “has not yet reached El Niño conditions,” but authorities are preparing in case the current heat and dry weather worsen.
“As of now, all preparedness measures are being undertaken by our department,” Aquino said.
Aquino said he had seen signs of dry conditions affecting corn and rice farms in parts of Banga and Surallah towns during his trips around the province.
He stressed that these were his observations and have yet to be backed by official data. The PDRRMO has yet to receive official report of farms being affected by the dry conditions.
“We are monitoring the agriculture sector, the health sector and, of course, our livestock that could be affected,” Aquino said.
He urged farmers to closely monitor weather forecasts and advisories from irrigation authorities as dry conditions persist.

Aquino said the province’s El Niño Task Force is already in place, bringing together the PDRRMO, Integrated Provincial Health Office, Provincial Veterinary Office, Bureau of Fire Protection and other concerned agencies.
He said resources are also available should the province need to respond to worsening conditions.
Part of the province’s Quick Response Fund remains available, along with other disaster funds that may be tapped for preparedness and response, Aquino said.

Gov. Reynaldo Tamayo Jr., who chairs the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council, has also directed officials to ensure that water impounding facilities are ready and relief supplies remain available in provincial warehouses, according to Aquino.
Fuel is also being secured for water pumps that may be needed if water supplies become affected.

Aquino said authorities are closely watching the effects of high temperatures on residents and have advised the public to avoid unnecessary exposure to the sun, stay hydrated and remain in cooler areas whenever possible.
The province’s preparations come after South Cotabato experienced severe dry conditions in late 2023 and early 2024 that caused widespread damage to farms and livelihoods.
South Cotabato declared a state of calamity on April 26, 2024, after agricultural and livelihood losses reached P201.9 million and affected at least 2,767 farmers.
Surallah, Tboli and Banga also declared states of calamity at the time as the dry spell affected farms and water supplies.

Aquino urged residents, particularly farmers and livestock raisers, to continue monitoring official advisories and take precautions as the province prepares for the possibility of more severe heat and dry conditions. /mr

articles.title: Grass fire burns 7 hectares of land in Southern Leyte town
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — A grass fire burned an estimated seven hectares of agricultural field and vegetation in three barangays of Hinunangan, Southern Leyte, with firefighters battling the blaze for…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — A grass fire burned an estimated seven hectares of agricultural field and vegetation in three barangays of Hinunangan, Southern Leyte, with firefighters battling the blaze for more than 10 hours before it was fully put off early Tuesday, Sept. 1.

The fire started at about 10:30 a.m. Monday, Aug. 31, in portions of Barangays Sto. Niño, Badiangaon and Manalog but was reported to authorities only at around 3:30 p.m., according to the Hinunangan Fire Station.

A responding team arrived at about 3:35 p.m. and immediately launched suppression and containment operations, with personnel from the Hinundayan Fire Station and the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office joining the firefighting effort.
The fire was placed under control at 1:40 a.m. Tuesday and declared completely put out at 2:10 a.m.
Authorities estimated the property damage at about P50,000. The affected agricultural lands and vegetation were reportedly owned or cultivated by six families.
No fatalities or injuries were reported, and the fire did not reach any residential houses or establishments.
Three fire trucks were deployed during the operation, which was led by FO3 Joselito Gomez, ground commander.

The Hinunangan Fire Station, under the leadership of SFO4 Michael Mamita, acting municipal fire marshal, reminded residents to exercise caution in activities that could trigger grass and vegetation fires.
The public was also urged to avoid indiscriminate burning and immediately report fire incidents to the nearest fire station or emergency responders. /mr

articles.title: Liechtenstein MPs vote to legalise abortion despite threat of veto
articles.summary: Organisers of the citizens' initiative say they have popular support, even though the all-powerful monarch has said he will veto the legislation.

blocks.text: Liechtenstein's parliament has narrowly backed a citizens' initiative to legalise abortion during the first 12 weeks of pregnancy.
The initiative, led by a group of women, would also lift a nationwide ban on providing information about abortions and make the procedure eligible for health insurance.

It was approved by 13 votes to 12 in the 25-seat parliament. However, it is unlikely to become law as the country's all-powerful ruler, Hereditary Prince Alois, has previously said he will veto the legislation.
Supporters of the bill say there is widespread backing in Liechtenstein to legalise abortion. However, MPs rejected a separate proposal to put the issue to a public vote.
Almost 80% of Liechtenstein's population of about 41,000 people belong to the Roman Catholic Church which is opposed to abortion.

The country last held a referendum on legalising abortion in 2011, when the proposal was rejected by 52% of voters. Hereditary Prince Alois had indicated at the time that he would have opposed the change.
Abortion is legal in most EU countries.
In Liechtenstein, it is allowed only in limited circumstances, including when a woman's life is at risk or a pregnancy is the result of rape.
Anyone who carries out an abortion outside those exceptions can face up to three years in prison, while a woman undergoing the procedure can be jailed for up to a year.

The current restrictions mean women have to go to other countries - mainly neighbouring Austria and Switzerland - to have an abortion. Since 2015, they have been able to do so without facing a penalty, but the cost is not covered by the health insurance.

The initiative to change the law was led by 28-year-old Tatjana As'Ad of the small left-wing Free List party. Supporters collected 4,970 signatures, nearly five times over the threshold needed to bring the proposal before parliament.
The proposed 12-week limit is already used in many European countries. In England, Scotland and Wales, it is legally available up to 23 weeks and six days under most circumstances.

articles.title: Yen soars as Bank of Japan tipped to raise interest rates
articles.summary: Jump lifts currency to highest level against dollar in a month, while global markets remain jittery

blocks.text: The Japanese yen has soared by more than 1.7% against the dollar amid speculation the Bank of Japan is set to raise interest rates.
The latest jump on Thursday lifted the yen to its highest level against the dollar in a month, at 155.85, and followed a 0.9% move the previous day.
Global markets remain jittery after this week’s dramatic government bond sell-off – caused by fears of a fresh inflation increase as a result of higher oil prices.
Investors have been reassessing their expectations for the future path of interest rates, in Japan and across other major economies.
Remarks by a Bank of Japan policymaker, Hajime Takata, suggesting it needs to move more “nimbly”, appeared to have heightened the prospects of a decisive move.

The chief executive of the financial adviser deVere, Nigel Green, said the scale of the yen appreciation over such a short time period underlined the febrile state of markets. “Markets this jumpy don’t need a shock to move hard, a rumour is enough,” he said.
Citi said in a note to clients: “(The) remarks are the strongest messaging we’ve heard from the board and reintroduces the idea of an expedited rate hike trajectory.”

The Bank of Japan has been incrementally raising rates for the past two years, after the economy finally shrugged off decades of deflation, or falling prices – but its main policy rate was left unchanged at 1% in July.
Markets now believe there is a 77% chance of a rate rise at the BoJ’s next meeting, which starts on 17 September.

Commenting on the latest market moves, Japan’s vice-finance minister for international affairs, Atsushi Mimura, said he was “neither satisfied nor reassured”, and policymakers “remain on a state of heightened alert”.
after newsletter promotion

The global bond market sell-off – pushing up the yield, or interest rate, on government borrowing – intensified earlier this week after the US Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, used a speech last Friday to indicate that he was determined to bring inflation back to target.

Warsh had previously baffled some investors by withdrawing the Fed’s approach of signalling future rate moves, known as “forward guidance” – but in Friday’s speech at the central bankers’ conference in Jackson Hole, he said that if inflation did not move towards the 2% target the Fed would have “more to do”.

The bond sell-off appeared to have eased on Thursday, with yields on 10-year UK government bonds, known as gilts, hovering at about 5.1% in morning trading – having touched the highest level since 2008, close to 5.3%, earlier this week.

articles.title: Dozens of trapped hydropower tunnel workers in Nepal could still be alive, official says
articles.summary: About 46 people believed to be trapped in ‘room-like’ structure inside hydro plant tunnel on Nepal-Tibet border
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu

blocks.text: Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber.
Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.

Most of the projects were destroyed when a surge of water, debris and mud came coursing down the river valley last week, triggered by ‌the collapse of a melting glacier on the border between Nepal and China-controlled Tibet.
The deadly flash floods reached up to 100mph (160km/h), according to scientists, and travelled more than 60 miles down the river valley, wiping away whole villages, bridges, and hydropower dams.
At least 1,252 people have been confirmed dead from the floods. More than 4,200 remain missing.

According to a preliminary estimate by the UN Development Programme, the disaster created at least 2.2m tonnes of debris, including parts of buildings, rocks and sediment. Large boulders and flood waters deluged the hydropower tunnels, blocking off the entrances, and some were buried deep in mud.

Rescue efforts have increasingly centred on these tunnels, where authorities believe workers may ⁠have survived for more than a week due to air pockets. So far, more than 270 people have been rescued from the hydropower projects.

blocks.caption: A turquoise-green house stands tall amid sludge near Trishuli River in the aftermath of flash floods.  Photograph: Arun Sankar/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Speaking on Wednesday, officials said they believed 46 people were still alive in an underground room in Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant, and efforts were ongoing to locate them using excavators and other heavy equipment.

“We are very confident that they must be alive after one week because … they have food and water over there in the building,” Amhsu Kiran Shahi, a board member of the Nepal ⁠electricity authority, told Reuters.

Durga Gurung, 60, said his brother Jhappad Bhujel was among those trapped in a hydropower tunnel. “Right now, we are just relying on God,” he told the Guardian. “We have not been given any information about whether the people inside are alive or not.

“Neither the army nor the people from the electricity authority are telling us anything. So many days have passed that we have reached a point where it feels like all we can do is hope for a miracle.”
“Our relatives are sitting inside a dark tunnel,” he added. “How long can they possibly survive?”

blocks.caption: The area around Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant before the flash flood.  Photograph: Maxar/DigitalGlobe/Getty Images

blocks.text: Major rescue operations were under way or planned at four hydropower projects. Two sites – the Rasuwagadhi hydroelectric project and the Upper Trishuli 3A facility – where about 90 people are missing, offered the strongest prospect of finding survivors because of the presence of air inside the tunnels, Shahi said.

The Rasuwagadhi hydroelectric project is located in Rasuwa district, about three miles away from the border with Tibet, which was one of the areas of Nepal hardest hit by the floods, and remains almost inaccessible except by helicopter. “This is the only project where it’s possible to walk through ‌the tunnel,” Shahi said. “The army tried doing that three days ago, but they didn’t find the room. We are going in again.”

At the Upper Trishuli 3A facility, another project hit by the floods, it took rescue workers almost six days to find the tunnels ⁠because of the thick mud. The authorities believe about 30 to 40 people may still be alive in the tunnel. “We are expecting [survivors] in there because we ​are told there is a ​dry space inside. We are ​trying to break into the tunnel now,” said the Nepali army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet on Wednesday.

The army said the search and rescue operation would go on for as long as there was hope for survivors, but that efforts would also continue to recover the dead bodies. “We are using every technology ​available in Nepal ‌right now, and we ​are taking help ​from the Indians, Chinese, Koreans. We have experts from Australia too,” added Basnet.

Families of those still trapped in the projects have returned to the Nepal electricity office for the past eight days, in the hope for information. Laxmi Adhikari’s brother Jeevanlal Adhikari had gone to the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project to test the machines, when the floods hit.

She accused the authorities of withholding information from the families, and of not acting fast enough to save their relatives. “We have been running from one ministry to another and from disaster management authority to another government office, trying to find my brother,” she said. “We keep going from place to place, but the rescue operation has not been accelerated.”

She said the lack of answers made the wait even more painful: “When the water came rushing in, where did he go? Did he manage to get to safety? They haven’t even given us definite information about whether our people are alive or not.”

Nepal has invested more than $9bn (£6.7bn) in building hydropower dams across the mountains, huge sums given the country’s small economy. According to preliminary surveys, the floods debilitated or destroyed 11 hydropower plants and knocked out about 10% of Nepal’s total electricity-generation capacity.
According to the authorities, more than 20,000 houses will have to be rebuilt in the aftermath of the flood. Nepal has put the cost of recovery at more than $5bn (£3.7bn).

articles.title: COA seeks to revise 11-year-old rules on auditing intelligence, confidential funds
articles.summary: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has exposed concerns and gaps in auditing confidential expenses

blocks.text: SECRET. Boxes labelled 'confidential funds,' containing documents being presented in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, are piled up in the Senate plenary hall on August 5, 2026.
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has exposed concerns and gaps in auditing confidential expenses

items: The Commission on Audit (COA) is seeking to revise Joint Circular No. 2015-001, which governs the auditing of intelligence and confidential funds, in light of issues raised during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Concerns highlighted include the lack of supporting documents for payments made with confidential funds, such as missing receipts and the use of aliases in acknowledgment receipts, which have drawn public scrutiny.

COA aims to establish clearer guidelines on handling confidential funds, including requirements for proof of payment, protecting informant identities, and ensuring proper documentation and coordination with other government agencies.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Commission on Audit (COA) Commissioner Michael Mallillin on Thursday, September 3, said the state auditor is seeking to revise Joint Circular No. 2015-001, which sets the guidelines for auditing intelligence and confidential funds.

The 11-year-old circular has been repeatedly cited in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. As Vice President and former education secretary, she allegedly misused millions of confidential funds in 2022 and 2023. The trial also exposed concerns and gaps in auditing confidential expenses.
One of the issues COA seeks to address is the supporting documents for proof of payment.

During the impeachment trial, the House prosecution questioned Duterte over the lack of receipts for payments made as rewards and payments for information. Duterte’s office submitted acknowledgment receipts as supporting documents for these payments.

The trial also revealed that Duterte’s Office of the Vice President also used confidential funds for medicine and food supplies, but provided no official receipts. State auditors standing as witnesses said they could not verify the authenticity of the purchases through acknowledgment receipts alone.

blocks.caption: How Sara Duterte broke rules on confidential funds — again and again

blocks.text: COA also wants to clarify how state auditors should handle aliases or code names, including whether their use should be allowed. The current circular does not specify whether aliases may be used.

The peculiar names in the acknowledgement receipts for the payment of information and rewards presented during impeachment trial, such as Mary Grace Piattos, Andy Lim, Alejandro Pikit, have drawn public attention and ridicule.
Duterte’s legal team, however, has neither confirmed nor denied whether the names on the receipts were fictitious.

blocks.caption: Andy C. Lim and Patty Ting? Kapunan brings 15 boxes of evidence, plenty of punchlines

blocks.text: Mallillin said the commission may set a requirement that would allow at least a state auditor to know the actual identities of the person, “as done in foreign jurisdictions.”
COA also seeks to address questions on the evidence of success and the causal links. Evidence of success is among the requirements for the payment of rewards and information using confidential funds.
The new guidelines also seek to protect the identity of informants.

“However, there should be a balance between protecting the identity but also a point of where COA, based on certain clearances, can actually take a look at the identity of the person without compromising national security and the confidentiality of the activity,” Mallillin said.
COA will also look into the storage of documents and the process of issuing credit notices and how disallowances should be addressed.
During the Senate budget hearing on COA, Mallillin said the commission would coordinate with other government agencies to update the guidelines.

The 2015 circular was crafted by COA, Department of Budget and Management, and Department of Interior and Local Government, Department of National Defense, and Governance Commission for Government-Owned and Controlled Corporations. – Rappler.com

articles.title: DOH: 6,253 leptospirosis cases logged as of August 29
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The number of leptospirosis cases in the country has risen to 6,253 as of Aug. 29, which is, however, 12 percent lower compared to cases in the same period last year, according…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The number of leptospirosis cases in the country has risen to 6,253 as of Aug. 29, which is, however, 12 percent lower compared to cases in the same period last year, according to the (DOH).

In a press briefing, Health Undersecretary Dr. Gloria Balboa once again warned the public against wading in floodwaters as she noted that cases of leptospirosis are expected to further rise in the next two weeks.
Leptospirosis is a disease caused by the bacteria Leptospira, and is transmitted to humans through contact with the urine of infected animals.
The DOH explained that the disease has an incubation period of five to 15 days.

Balboa said around 1 percent of all leptospirosis cases in the country are considered as severe. A total of 378 deaths caused by the disease have been recorded nationwide from Jan. 4 to Aug. 29, she said.
The health undersecretary urged the public to immediately visit the nearest health center if they are exposed to floodwaters so that they can get the appropriate treatment.

“When you are exposed, within 72 hours is the [period] during which taking doxycycline will be effective, but you need to consult first because there are proper instructions [in taking the medicine],” Balboa said in Filipino, referring to the antibiotic used to treat leptospirosis.
She said that those with leptospirosis will first experience symptoms such as fever followed by chills.

Once the infection spreads to the liver, this will cause yellowing of the eyes or skin. If it reaches the kidney, the infected individual would have dark colored urine and may even need to undergo dialysis.
“Let’s not wait for that,” Balboa said.
“At the first sign of a symptom, whatever you feel, even if it’s just an ordinary fever, you need to get a check-up, because the progression of this illness is also very fast.”
She assured that hospitals are prepared amid the increase in leptospirosis cases, noting that guidelines on the implementation of a “surge capacity plan” have already been established.
This includes transferring patients to other hospitals or assigning additional health workers if needed.

Balboa added that some patients may also be referred to private hospitals since their treatment will be covered by the Philippine Health Insurance Corp., whose benefit package for leptospirosis has been increased to a maximum of P411,000.
Moreover, she also urged employers to provide personal protective equipment to their workers to ensure that they will be protected from leptospirosis. /gsg

articles.title: Palace: DPWH eyes review of ‘Aquino-Singson flood control master plan’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon is eyeing a possible review of the “Aquino-Singson Master Plan” as part of the government’s efforts to address the country’s flooding problem,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon is eyeing a possible review of the “Aquino-Singson Master Plan” as part of the government’s efforts to address the country’s flooding problem, according to Palace press officer and Undersecretary Claire Castro.
In a briefing on Thursday, Castro said the master plan could be used alongside the Department of Public Works and Highways’ (DPWH) separate master plan for major river basins.
The masterplan that Castro was referring to is the one crafted under former Public Works Secretary Rogelio Singson, who headed the DPWH when former president Benigno Aquino III was still in office.

“Iyan po ay pagsasama-samahin at titingnan, at kailangan na po ring i-update. At ang sabi nga rin po ng Pangulo sa nakaraang pagpupulong, kailangan na ring i-update kung ano ang dapat na gawin nang naaayon na po sa maaaring epekto ng climate change,” Castro said.

(That will be consolidated and reviewed, and it also needs to be updated. As the President said during the previous meeting, we also need to update what needs to be done in accordance with the possible effects of climate change.)
The Aquino administration approved a long-term, P351-billion flood management master plan in 2012 made during the time of Singson at DPWH.
However, this was not carried out by the administration of former President Rodrigo Duterte.
Asked why the master plan had not been implemented during the first four years of the Marcos administration, Castro said she could not speak on behalf of previous officials.

“Ang akin lamang masasagot ay kung ano po ang ginagawa ngayon ni Secretary Vince Dison dahil sa pinaabot niya sa atin ginagawa niya po sa ngayon ang lahat ng mga imprastraktura base sa master plan ng major river basins,” she said.

(Ang akin lamang masasagot ay kung ano po ang ginagawa ngayon ni Secretary Vince Dison dahil sa pinaabot niya sa atin ginagawa niya po sa ngayon ang lahat ng mga imprastraktura base sa master plan ng major river basins. )

Moreover, the Palace official clarified President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s statement on Wednesday that the country had a “master plan” for flood control for decades but that it had never been implemented.
“Ang pinapatungkulan po dito ng Pangulo ay nakita po ng mga eksperto rin na may mga masterplans na noon na dahil sa hindi naisagawa, nagkakaroon ito ngayon ng epekto sa pagbabaha,” Castro said.

(What the President was referring to is that experts have also observed that there were master plans in the past that, because they were not implemented, are now contributing to the flooding we are experiencing.)

“So, ang Pangulo po ngayon ay gumagawa ng mga proyekto, lalung-lalo na sa ilalim ng pamumuno ni Secretary Vince Dizon. So, kung ano po iyong hawak natin ngayon especially itong sa major river basins, iyan po iyong inuuna ng Pangulo para po maibsan iyong epekto ng sobrang pagbabaha or taas ng tubig kapag malakas po ang ulan o mayroon pong bagyo,” she continued.

(So, the President is now undertaking projects, particularly under the leadership of Secretary Vince Dizon. What we currently have, especially the plans for the major river basins, are what the President is prioritizing in order to mitigate the effects of severe flooding or rising water levels during heavy rains or typhoons.)
The government is also willing to make the national flood control master plan public as part of its transparency efforts. /mr

articles.title: Parked passenger boat sinks in waters off Calayan town in Cagayan
articles.summary: TUGUEGARAO CITY – A passenger boat that was moored near Calayan town in Cagayan province was sunk by strong waves on Wednesday (Sept. 2) but no one was hurt. A worker at the boat, who tried to…

blocks.text: TUGUEGARAO CITY – A passenger boat that was moored near Calayan town in Cagayan province was sunk by strong waves on Wednesday (Sept. 2) but no one was hurt.
A worker at the boat, who tried to save his belongings, is safe, said Jeo Robert Arirao, a rescue officer of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, in an interview.

The boat, M/B Lance, was not ferrying passengers due to the prevailing monsoon rains and the threat of Typhoon Pilandok. It had been secured at the shoreline of Barangay Magsidel at Calayan town when the waves filled the boat with water.
On Thursday (Sept. 3), volunteers helped each other tie drums to the sunken boat in order to lift it and pull it to shore.
Sea travel has been restricted by the coast guard due to the gusty winds and strong waves. /mr

articles.title: Dy’s focus on work helps House rebuild people’s trust – Hernandez
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The improved trust and performance ratings of the House of Representatives reflect the focus it has devoted to legislation and public service under the leadership of Speaker…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The improved trust and performance ratings of the House of Representatives reflect the focus it has devoted to legislation and public service under the leadership of Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III, Senior Deputy Speaker Rep. Ferdinand “Dinand” L. Hernandez said in a statement on Thursday.
“This is an encouraging sign that the Filipino people are beginning to see and appreciate the work being done by the House under the leadership of Speaker Bojie Dy,” Hernandez said.

He was referring to the latest OCTA Research Tugon ng Masa survey, which showed that public trust in the House increased from 36 percent in the first quarter of 2026 to 38 percent in the second quarter. Distrust fell by five percentage points, from 33 percent to 28 percent.
Satisfaction with the House performance also rose from 35 percent to 37 percent, while dissatisfaction declined from 35 percent to 32 percent.

“The speaker has never been one to seek praise or make grand claims about what we have accomplished. His approach has always been simple: Keep our heads down, focus on the work, and allow the results to speak for themselves. As he said in one LegisHear in Isabela: With or without a survey, we will work.”
Hernandez said the survey results should further motivate the House to keep working, considering that a significant number of Filipinos remained undecided about its performance.

“We are grateful for the improvement, but our work is far from finished. Trust is something we must earn every day through the passage of meaningful laws and the delivery of concrete results,” he said.
He credited Speaker Dy for keeping the House focused on legislation while pursuing reforms to make itself “more transparent, responsive, and accountable.”

Under Dy’s leadership, he pointed out, the House has already approved 28 measures identified as priorities by the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council, as these are aimed at addressing the country’s most urgent economic and social needs.

“Every day, it seems that another important measure is moving out of committee and closer to passage. The House is moving, the committees are working, and important legislation is being acted upon. In my view, the direction of the speaker—that focus on the job at hand—has helped us regain some of the public’s confidence,” Hernandez said.
The entire House, including its staff, should be credited for its improved public perception, he stressed.

“Speaker Dy himself would be the first to say that this is not the achievement of one person. This reflects the collective work of the entire House and our shared commitment to build a Congress—isang Bagong Kongreso—that listens, acts, and delivers,” Hernandez said.
The OCTA Research survey was conducted from July 4 to 11 among 1,200 adult respondents nationwide and has a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points. /atm

articles.title: MILF sacks Macacua as military chief, dismisses 40 other commanders
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY — The central committee of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) stripped Bangsamoro interim Chief Minister Abdulraof “Sammy Gambar” Macacua of his rank as chief of its…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY — The central committee of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) stripped Bangsamoro interim Chief Minister Abdulraof “Sammy Gambar” Macacua of his rank as chief of its military arm, the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces (BIAF).
The panel cited insubordination as the reason. The dismissal of Macacua was done in front of a large number of MILF members and supporters, including heavily armed fighters.
Sheikh Abdulmanan Kitugi, a member of the MILF central committee, announced the removal of Macacua and over 40 MILF base commanders, deputy commanders and middle-level officers.
The pronouncement was made during the MILF-BIAF general assembly at the front’s main headquarters in Camp Darapanan, Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao del Norte.

Macacua and the field commanders were suspended indefinitely in June due to their alleged insubordination and for allegedly holding activities without the written or verbal approval from the MILF central committee.
As Sheik Kitugi announced the firing of Macacua, the crowd in attendance reacted with a strong chant of “Allahu Akbar.”
The audience, mostly members of BIAF, chanted the same every time the names of the removed officers were read.
Engr. Mohajirin Ali, MILF spokesperson, told reporters that Macacua and the field commanders were only stripped of their positions, but they remained members of the MILF.
Macacua had said that it is okay with him if he is removed as BIAF chief.
“But it’s another story if I am removed as an MILF member without due process,” he noted.
Speaking during the assembly, MILF chair Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim rallied all members of the MILF and the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), the front’s political party.
The MILF, through the UBJP, is seeking seats in the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) on Sept. 14.

“We paid blood. We lost the lives of our fighters to achieve this genuine autonomy. Let us not allow this to go away. You are the next generation and you must reap the fruit of our struggle,” Ebrahim said in Maguindanaoan language.
“Let us fight for this autonomy, this BARMM, through the ballot for the next generation. We deserve this autonomy. Let us defend it so our next generation will enjoy it,” he added.
Ebrahim takes on the role of BIAF chief in concurrent capacity.
For his part, MILF vice chair Mohagher Iqbal called on all members of the MILF and the UBJP and their families to vote for the party and its candidates in the historic polls.
“Let us do everything we can to win the election, but we must do so peacefully. Let us not become criminals. We must not resort to violence, and we will not allow violence to take place,” Iqbal said.
In his previous media interviews, Iqbal said the MILF, especially its military arm, will “never initiate or start gun-related violence during, before and after the regional balloting.”

“Definitely, the MILF will not start using violence. If there would be any, it will not come from the MILF. That is what I assure you,” he told reporters during a UBJP assembly in BARMM’s Special Geographic Area (SGA). /apl

articles.title: Ramon Ang: Bulacan flooding due to low elevation, narrow rivers
articles.summary: BULAKAN, Bulacan— Lowland elevation, narrow and winding rivers and low bridges are to blame for floods in the coastal municipality of Bulakan and not the New Manila International Airport (NMIA)…

blocks.text: BULAKAN, Bulacan— Lowland elevation, narrow and winding rivers and low bridges are to blame for floods in the coastal municipality of Bulakan and not the New Manila International Airport (NMIA) project of developer San Miguel Corporation (SMC) that will rise here, the company’s President Ramon S. Ang said at a news conference on Tuesday (Sept 1).

He was reacting to assertions made a day earlier at the “Kilos Bulacan” Rally, organized by 34 Bulacan people’s organizations, which pushed for government action to curb the floods that annually engulfs 23 towns and cities, including a demand to end all reclamation projects.
The groups listed SMC’s airport and aeropolis among projects they want stopped during their Aug. 31 protest near the Bulacan Capitol.

Obet Rodrigo, a resident of Bulakan’s Cupang Maysantol and one of the conveners of Kilos Bulacan, accused the SMC project of blocking all the rivers in the town which supposedly triggered the backflow of water that routinely floods his community.

“Water flows in all directions and does not look for geographical boundaries. Look at (the Bulacan towns of) Guiguinto and Balagtas, their waterways should flow down to the Taliptip river. The waters from Sta. Maria (town), the City of San Jose del Monte, Obando (town) and the City of Meycauayan should flow towards Tawiran (barangay), in the boundary of our town and Obando but the waters have been blocked,” Rodrigo told the Inquirer.

Ang said: “Bulakan (lands are) really low. Even when there is no rain, many areas there are flooded (because of the tidal waters from Manila Bay). Even bridges are also low, and houses are built along the rivers and (are) serving as river blockade. Roads are being upgraded but not the residential areas,” the SMC president said.

If asked for a solution, Ang said SMC would elevate the residential areas. “If we would be allowed in partnership with the local government, we would upgrade the low-lying areas where the houses are situated. By area alisin muna natin ang bahay, tambakan natin at saka natin sila pabalikin (we would remove the houses, backfill to elevate the land and then we bring back the houses) ,” he said.

“The Bulacan airport (in Bulakan) is beside the Manila Bay and is surrounded by big rivers and these rivers around (the future airport and economic suburb) have water level gauges. The waters there do not rise, meaning that is not causing flood,” Ang said.
The project site was solid ground “before it was turned into fishponds, ” he said.

Ang said: “Years later, we acquired them and we refilled them with soil again. It was originally proposed for an airport by the late former Bulacan Representative Teodulo Natividad. The area is the best location, the best site for an airport because of the wind direction. Other areas have crosswind but not the site in Bulakan. The place has a favorable wind condition for an airport.”

Ang also dismissed claims that SMC blocked three river systems. “There is no truth to what our rivals and enemies in business are saying. They are just merely rumors and are not true. I did show you the video of the location of the airport, the maps, the cleaning and clearing we did. But here comes one person starting rumors that the airport is not a good project. The (individual who is) against the project is hiding under a fake name. That is AI, making up stories,” he said.
Kilos Bulacan’s statement says: “Blaming the people’s waste and the groundwater extraction as the source of the flooding is avoiding the truth.”

On Thursday (September 3), Bulacan Gov. Daniel Fernando met with the Department of Public Works and Highways to discuss measures that would further strengthen ongoing river dredging and flood clearing operations, along with the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) and the Bulacan Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office (PDRRMO).

Fernando had ordered the purchase of additional suction equipment, water pumps, backhoes and barges to clear national and local drainage canals of obstructions like garbage which have been preventing water to flow freely.
Manuel Lukban Jr., head of the Bulacan PDRRMO said an initial estimate puts the cost of the equipment at P75 million.
The government would also address flood river walls which are unfinished and ineffective culverts.
Vice Gov. Alexis Castro had asked the DPWH for a copy of the submitted projects under the 2027 National Expenditure Program. /mr

articles.title: Longer brownouts, worsening haze batter Metro Cebu
articles.summary: CEBU CITY — Metro Cebu grappled with two crises on Thursday as a nine-hour red alert over the Visayas power grid coincided with “acutely unhealthy” air quality. These developments prompted Gov.…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY — Metro Cebu grappled with two crises on Thursday as a nine-hour red alert over the Visayas power grid coincided with “acutely unhealthy” air quality.

These developments prompted Gov. Pamela Baricuatro to convene power stakeholders while environmental officials monitored the deteriorating haze, which forced hundreds of students and teachers to shift to online classes because of health concerns.

“While electricity generation, transmission, and distribution are not directly under the jurisdiction of the Cebu Provincial Government, I have called for a meeting with our power suppliers and key energy stakeholders … to get a clear picture of the present situation, understand where the gaps are, and determine what can be done immediately and in the longer term,” she said.
The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) placed the Visayas grid again under a Red Alert from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m. Thursday, one of the longest red-alert periods in recent months.
Available capacity stood at 2,187 megawatts (MW) against a peak demand of 2,575 MW, resulting in a 388-MW supply deficit.
NGCP attributed the shortage to 579.1 MW lost to forced power plant outages and another 212.9 MW unavailable because of plants operating at reduced capacity.
As a result, the rotational brownouts here have stretched from one hour to as long as 2.5 hours.
Distributor firm Visayan Electric Company (VECO) said the power interruptions were caused entirely by generation and transmission shortages, not problems within its distribution network.
The utility also warned customers that rotational outages could continue.

“We understand the inconvenience this situation may cause our customers. Visayan Electric is coordinating closely with the relevant grid authorities and will keep the public informed as the situation develops, while we continue to do our part in managing demand within our franchise area,” VECO president and general manager Engr. Mark Anthony Kindica said.
The utility also urged households and businesses to voluntarily conserve electricity during peak alert hours.
Air quality worsens
While the power situation deteriorated, air quality in Metro Cebu also worsened.
The Environmental Management Bureau in Central Visayas (EMB-7) recorded an air quality index of 252 on Thursday, a level classified as “very unhealthy” under standard air-quality classifications.
The worsening haze has already disrupted classes, with schools shifting to online learning as officials monitor the potential health risks from the poor air quality.
Energy summit

Baricuatro also announced a Cebu Energy Summit on Oct. 7 that will bring together representatives from the energy sector, government, business and investment groups to discuss the province’s long-term power needs.

She cited renewable energy projects the provincial government has helped facilitate, including the ACCIONA solar farm in Daanbantayan and Alternergy’s wind project. She also pointed to the Alegria oil and gas exploration site, which she said could eventually become a power source.

“We want more investments. We want industries to expand. We want more businesses and more jobs for Cebuanos. But none of these can happen sustainably if our energy supply cannot keep pace with our growth,” Baricuatro said. /mr

articles.title: Kenyan president orders crackdown on foreigners operating small businesses
articles.summary: It comes amid concerns over the growing number of traders from neighbouring countries.

blocks.text: Kenya's President William Ruto has ordered a crackdown on foreigners operating small-scale businesses, saying local traders and hawkers need to be protected.
His announcement comes amid growing debate about the increasing number of African migrants involved in Kenya's vast informal economy.
"From next week, all [foreign] traders doing those small businesses should close them," he said, also promising to fast-track proposed legislation to preclude foreigners from certain areas of trade.

Ruto said Kenya remained open to foreign investment, but argued that investors - including Chinese traders - should create jobs and expand production rather than compete with Kenyans in small businesses.

"It cannot be that a person comes from China or elsewhere to be a hawker or open a small shop," he said in an address to small-scale traders who had come to meet the president at State House in the capital, Nairobi, on Wednesday afternoon.
"We have made efforts to improve the economy, we have not improved investor confidence for hawkers to come to Kenya," said Ruto, who plans to seek a second term in election next year.
It is unclear how many foreign nationals are involved in small-scale trading or how many would be affected by the new crackdown.
Kenya hosts a large refugee population, some of whom live and work outside the country's refugee camps.
Government figures show that Kenya had about 857,000 registered refugees and asylum seekers by the end of June, with nearly 14% living in urban areas.

Kenyan law recognises the right of refugees to work and operate businesses, although they are required to obtain the appropriate documentation. Refugees wishing to work or engage in a trade or business can apply for a special permit.

In Nairobi and other major towns, migrants from the region can be found working in barber shops and salons, construction, operating motorbike taxis and street vending, as well as selling clothes, food and household goods.

Some have fled conflicts or economic hardship at home, while others have moved to Kenya in search of better opportunities under the relatively free movement of people allowed within the East African Community, a regional bloc made up of eight countries.
The growing presence of foreigners has at times caused tensions with local traders and workers who accuse them of competing for scarce jobs and business opportunities.
In July, a video of a Kenyan man confronting a Burundian trader in Nairobi and accusing him of taking opportunities from locals sparked widespread criticism.
The clash also prompted Fred Ngoga, an expert on regional conflict prevention from Burundi, to appeal for the protection of his country's citizens.

"The majority of Kenyans are decent and good people who welcome their brothers and sisters from Burundi," he said at the time, adding that most Kenyans had rejected the hostility directed at the trader.
Kenya's foreign ministry also sought to reassure Burundians and other East Africans living in the country following the incident.
While Ruto's latest move is likely to prove controversial given Kenya's status as regional economic hub, it also comes amid wider concerns about xenophobia elsewhere in Africa.

This year South Africa has seen a wave of protests about undocumented migrants - and tens of thousands of Africans there have opted to be repatriated voluntarily, some saying they have been the targets of intimidation and attacks.

articles.title: IN NUMBERS: First BARMM parliamentary elections
articles.summary: Here are all the numbers you need to know about the first-ever BARMM parliamentary elections

blocks.text: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is about to elect its parliament for the first time. It will mark the Bangsamoro people’s third attempt at regional governance.

The landmark vote was originally scheduled for 2022, but at least four postponements in May 2022, May 2025, October 2025, and again in March 2026 pushed back the polls and extended the region’s initial three-year transition period to roughly seven years.

Now, over 600 candidates are vying for seats in the 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament to be elected on September 14. More than 2.3 million registered voters are set to decide the outcome of these historic — but highly contested — polls.

The elections are happening as tensions continue to heighten within the upper ranks of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), whose members currently have a guaranteed majority in the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) or the BARMM’s interim regional government.
Here are all the numbers you need to know about the first-ever BARMM parliamentary elections.
2.3 million registered voters
A total of 2,393,202 people registered to vote in the upcoming BARMM parliamentary elections.

Lanao del Sur has the largest voting population, with 727,546 registered voters, making up 30.4% of the voting population. This is followed by Maguindanao del Sur with 469,114 voters and Maguindanao del Norte with 419,365 voters.
These votes will decide who fills the 80 seats in the region’s first elected Bangsamoro Parliament.
679 candidacies filed for 80 seats

A total of 679 candidates filed to run in the BARMM parliamentary elections. While one regional party with 40 candidates — the Moro Ako Party — had its registration canceled over alleged misrepresentation, it remains on the ballots.
Out of the 679 candidates represented on the ballots, 454 are running as party representatives, 107 as district representatives, and 78 as sectoral representatives.
The 80-seat Bangsamoro Parliament is composed of:

items: 40 party representatives, who will be elected through a proportional representation system
32 district representatives, who will represent BARMM’s parliamentary districts
8 sectoral representatives reserved for women, youth, traditional leaders, ulama, settler communities, and other sectors

blocks.text: The two representatives for the non-Moro indigenous peoples were already elected on August 25, ahead of the September 14 polls. This is because the Bangsamoro Organic Law requires NMIP representatives to be elected using a unique selection process that “adhere[s] to their customary laws and indigenous processes.”
Nearly 70% of candidates are men
An estimated 7 in every 10 candidates in the BARMM parliamentary race are men.
Of the 678 candidates whose genders were declared, 468 are male (68.92%) and 210 are female (30.93%).
The share of women candidates barely surpasses the 30% threshold set for party nominees under the Bangsamoro Electoral Code.

For the party-seat race, 12 of the 13 parties that submitted nominee lists met the 30% requirement, according to election watchdog Legal Network for Truthful Elections (LENTE). Only the Indigenous, Settlers, Sama and Minorities Alliance Party did not fulfill the requirement, though they filed only a total of 14 candidates.
The parties nominated an average of 13 to 14 women each, although the proportion varied across slates. But LENTE pointed out that majority of the women were ranked lower in nominee lists.
The gender gap shifts in other races. There are only 14 female candidates for district representatives as against 93 males, while the sectoral race has 24 female candidates to 54 males.
38% of candidates are Gen X
Generation X candidates, or those currently aged 46 to 61 years old, make up the largest share of the field with 261 candidates. After them, there are 174 millennials and 170 baby boomers.
There are also 52 Gen Z candidates running for seats, along with 3 candidates from the Silent Generation.

The oldest candidate in the pool is 82 years old, while the youngest is 18. The Bangsamoro Organic Law requires parliament members to be at least 25 years old on the day of the election, except for youth representatives who must be 18 to 30 years old.
34% of candidates from Maguindanao del Norte

Maguindanao del Norte accounts for the largest share of candidates in the BARMM parliamentary race. Of the 678 candidates, 229, or about 34%, come from the province. Lanao del Sur followed with 202 candidates, then Tawi-Tawi with 80, and Basilan with 75. Maguindanao del Sur has 67 candidates, while 26 are from the Special Geographic Area.

The high number of candidates is matched by the province’s outsized role in the region’s politics. The Bangsamoro Parliament designated Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, as the seat of the Bangsamoro government under Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 37. The government center is being established in Barangay Sarmiento in the same municipality.

But Maguindanao del Norte’s political weight predates the new government center. The province is closely tied to the MILF and its political arm, the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) — a major force in BARMM politics.
UBJP, BFP field about 23% of the whole candidate pool

Across all the COCs filed for the upcoming elections, a total of 29 different political parties were named, though only 16 applied for accreditation. Out of those 16, 13 fielded candidates for party representatives.

There are 23 candidates running independently, based on their COCs, including the BTA’s Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, who was stripped of his positions under the MILF after a falling out with UBJP members over his appointment in 2025.

The UBJP fielded the largest total number of candidates, with 81 total across the three different races. It is followed by the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) — now chaired by Macacua, despite still being listed as an independent candidate on the ballots. BFP has a total of 74 candidates.
Candidates from these two parties accounted for 22.83% of the total number of candidacies filed for the BARMM elections.
Other parties with sizable slates include the BARMM Grand Coalition (57 candidates), Bangsamoro Party (55 candidates), and Bangsamoro Empowerment and Social Transformation Party (45 candidates).
Family names shaping the BARMM candidate pool

Some surnames and middle names appear repeatedly among those seeking seats in the Bangsamoro Parliament. Clan and dynastic politics have been a prominent threat to the electoral process and the BARMM’s development as a whole, an issue repeatedly raised by watchdog groups.

Usman and Abubakar each appear nine times, the most out of the candidate pool. This is no coincidence, as the Usmans are an MILF-affiliated clan and the Abubakars are also a powerful family mainly based in Sulu, which used to be part of the BARMM.

Other notable clans and dynasties whose names repeatedly cropped up in candidacies include the Ampatuans and Midtimbangs of Maguindanao, the Alonto-Adiongs of Lanao del Sur, and the Sali clan of Tawi-Tawi.
108 election areas of concern
Heightened security risks because of the BARMM elections prompted the Commission on Elections (Comelec) to place 108 areas under watch.
The categories classify the threat levels in each area as follows:

items: Green – areas with no reported security concerns or that are considered relatively peaceful and orderly
Yellow – areas where there have been recent suspected election-related incidents, intense partisan political rivalries, or a history of being placed under Comelec control
Orange – areas with serious armed threats or two or more of the security concerns in the yellow category

Red – areas with the highest level of concern, where there are one or more security concerns from the yellow category, serious armed threats, or if there are grounds for the declaration of Comelec control (e.g., the presence of paramilitary forces and private armies; fraud or other election irregularities in past elections)

blocks.text: Lanao del Sur — where the 2017 Marawi siege happened — has 40 areas of concern, the highest number of such areas in the region. This is followed by Maguindanao del Sur with 24 and Maguindanao del Norte with 13.
Fears over election violence are particularly prevalent in the BARMM, given the region’s long history of violence.

blocks.caption: Blood, rebellion, and uneasy peace: The Bangsamoro’s unfinished journey

blocks.text: Ahead of the September elections, watchdog groups like Climate Conflict Action Asia have warned about a broader surge in violence targeting state security forces in the region. (READ MORE: Extremists blamed for deadly ambush as monitor flags attack surge in BARMM)

Even in the 2025 national elections and the 2023 barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections, BARMM accounted for most of the areas of concern in the country. – with reports from Lance Magno, Cyrene Sancon, Kristine Santillan, and Angel Cesa/Rappler.com
Ava Dumaup, Lance Magno, Cyrene Sancon, Kristine Santillan, and Angel Cesa are interns and volunteers of Rappler’s Research and Data unit.

The Ombudsman says Jesus Fernandez allegedly received a P14.7-million bribe for the said project

items: The Office of the Ombudsman filed corruption cases against former Bureau of Fire Protection chief Jesus Fernandez for alleged irregularities in a P485.6-million ambulance procurement.

Fernandez is accused of receiving P14.752 million in bribes and has been dismissed from government service, facing penalties including cancellation of government eligibility and forfeiture of retirement benefits.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman filed corruption cases against a former Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) chief and dismissed him from government service over alleged irregularities in the procurement of P485.6 million worth of ambulances.

The Ombudsman announced on Thursday, September 3, that it filed cases for two counts of indirect bribery and two counts of alleged violation of Section 3(b) of Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act against former BFP chief Jesus Fernandez with the Sandiganbayan.
Apart from Fernandez, the Ombudsman also said it filed two counts of corruption of public officials against joint venture representative Rosaverna Sangga, who’s involved in the procurement.

The cases stemmed from a complaint filed by the Department of the Interior and Local Government, which probed the BFP’s procurement of 132 units of type 1 basic life support ambulances. The contract was given to Toyota Mabolo, which entered into a joint venture agreement with Autozone Prime Distributors, Inc.
According to the Ombudsman, Fernandez allegedly received P14.752 million from Sangga. The BFP chief was then chairperson of the bids and awards committee (BAC).

“Sangga delivered Ten Million Seven Hundred Fifty Two Thousand Pesos (Php10,752,000.00) on 21 November 2024, and Four Million Pesos (Php4,000,000.00) on 25 September 2025 to FDir. Fernandez,” the Ombudsman said.
Amid the probe into Fernandez, the Marcos administration appointed Fire Chief Superintendent Wilberto Rico Neil Kwan Tiu as BFP officer-in-charge.

blocks.caption: How BFP chief allegedly got P14.75-M kickback from ambulance deal

blocks.text: Meanwhile, in the separate administrative case, the Ombudsman said it found the former BFP chief guilty of conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service and grave misconduct.
This administrative conviction carries not only the penalty of dismissal from government service against Fernandez, but also the following punishments:

items: Cancellation of government eligibility
Forfeiture of retirement benefits
Perpetual disqualification from reemployment in government service

blocks.text: According to the Ombudsman, it was found in the administrative case that Fernandez’s act of allegedly receiving money was against his duties and responsibilities as BFP chief and BAC chairperson. It added that this undermined the integrity expected from his office.

“He is not merely an officer of the BFP. He is the Fire Chief of the agency. He was the BAC Chairman when he received the SOP on 21 November 2024 and the Head of the Procuring Entity when he received the second SOP on 25 September 2025,” the Ombudsman said.

“Receiving any gift, compensation, promise, or consideration from any individual in relation to his position gives the appearance of impropriety, which not only [brings] doubt to his credibility but significantly tarnishes the credibility of the agency that he leads, in this case, especially in the process of procurement,” it added. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: Toronto mayor to speak after city hammered by powerful summer storm

Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow is expected to speak Thursday morning after the city and surrounding areas were slammed by high winds and torrential rains that damaged buildings, flooded roads and left thousands without power.
The Latest

items: The Greater Toronto Area is cleaning up a day after a heavy thunderstorm damaged buildings, closed roads and knocked out power.
Toronto Hydro said early today roughly 8,300 customers were still without power. The province's Crown-owned power supplier, Hydro One, said more than 58,000 customers are without power.

Several major roads remain closed, including the Gardiner Expressway, Bayview Avenue and parts of the northbound Don Valley Parkway. In Vaughan, Ont., Huntington Road is closed indefinitely because of a large sinkhole.
Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow is scheduled to provide an update on the storm response at 9:30 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Zubiri addresses criticisms amid 'tired' remark
articles.summary: Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri on Thursday shrugged off criticisms on social media after he said that he was exhausted supposedly because he has to work for 12 hours a day amid the hectic…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 6:44pm

Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri on Thursday shrugged off criticisms on social media after he said that he was exhausted supposedly because he has to work for 12 hours a day amid the hectic schedule at the upper chamber.

At a press conference, Zubiri explained that he was merely expressing what he felt during that time, pointing out that the Senate is simultaneously handling budget hearings, regular sessions, and the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

“Kasi ako, I'm very candid so I just tell them how I feel. Kaya naiipit ako minsan… No [I’m not complaining]. I’m being honest. It doesn't matter kung pagod na pagod ako, gagawin namin ang aming tungkulin bilang senador at impeachment court judges,” he said.

(I'm very candid so I just tell them how I feel. That's why I get criticized sometimes. No, I'm not complaining. I'm being honest. It doesn't matter if I'm really tired, we will do our duty as senators and as impeachment court judges.)

“If we have to work 24/7, gagawin namin 24/7. Binanggit ko lang ang aking present condition at that time. Kasi nga napakahirap i-juggle lahat ng tatlong napakahalagang…activities ng Senate,” he added.
(If we have to work 24/7, we will do so. I just mentioned my present condition at that time. Because it's very difficult to juggle all three very important…activities in the Senate.)
Netizens lashed out at Zubiri after he made a manifestation on the 21st day of the impeachment trial, saying he was “pagod na pagod” (very tired) as he has to work from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Currently, the Senate holds the impeachment trial from Monday to Wednesday, which starts at 10 a.m. and usually ends nearly 3 p.m., sometimes extending until 4 p.m. After the trial, the plenary session is conducted until early evening or until when the senators tackle all the legislative agenda for the day.
Thursdays and Fridays are usually reserved for hearings, including the deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.
Robin defends
Senator Robin Padilla also defended Zubiri amid the backlash, saying that what the majority leader said was not a complaint, but a “reality shared” by all of the senators.

“Kailanman po ay hindi nagreklamo si Senator Migz Zubiri patungkol sa aming trabaho. Ang tawag nga namin sa kanya ay ang ‘trabahador ng taongbayan sa Senado!’ Ang kanyang sinambit na pagod na pagod na siya ay hindi po isang pagrereklamo kundi ang katotohanan naming lahat,” Padilla said in a Facebook post.

“Napakasipag na tao ni Senator Migz! Ang ibig lamang niyang sabihin at iparating ay kung paano namin mapagkakasya ang oras, araw, at ang isang linggo sa patong-patong na trabaho na may masusing pag-aaral,” he added.
(Senator Migz is a very hardworking person! What he simply meant to convey was how we could manage our time to handle all the workload that requires thorough study.) — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: CHR gets zero capital outlay in proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: The CHR had originally proposed a budget of P2.74 billion, which was finalized at P1.27 billion in the NEP, the nominated budget of the executive branch. CHR chairperson Richard Palpal-latoc said…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 6:42pm
The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) received zero capital outlay in the National Expenditure Program (NEP), as well as a drastic reduction in its proposed budget.

The CHR had originally proposed a budget of P2.74 billion, which was finalized at P1.27 billion in the NEP, the nominated budget of the executive branch. CHR chairperson Richard Palpal-latoc said that this was a 53% reduction from what the agency wanted.

“Bagama't zero po yung aming capital outlay, patuloy pa rin naman po ang komisyon sa pagtupad sa kanyang tungkulin at mandato. Gayunpaman, dahil wala pong allocation for the capital outlay, maapektuhan ang aming serbisyo in terms of ICT (Information and communications technology), yung aming mga infrastructure facilities, workplace, so of course kailangan ng aming mga empleyado ng maayos na workplaces, lalong-lalo na yung mga regional offices, yun po maapektuhan po siya,” Palpal-latoc said.

(Even if our capital outlay is zero, the commission will still carry out its duty and mandate. But because there is no allocation for the capital outlay, our services will be affected in terms of ICT, our infrastructure facilities, workplace; so of course, our employees need proper workplaces, especially in our regional offices, that could be affected.)
The capital outlay is the budget used for the purchase of long-term goods and services.
House lawmakers in the Committee on Appropriations lamented the reduction.

“Ang budget ang pinaka-concrete expression of priority and in this case, given the massive cut in the proposed and the actual NEP proposed budget, mukhang hindi talaga priority ng administrasyong into ang human rights,” Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña said.

(The budget is the most concrete expression of priority and in this case, given the massive cut in the proposed and the actual NEP proposed budget, it looks like human rights is not a priority for this administration.)
Cendaña also raised that the CHR was asking for an additional budget outside the NEP to pay job order personnel.

Palpal-latoc said that the CHR would still be able to pay these workers, but it would take away money from the Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses. This would impact the operating expenses. Instead of the budget going into regular activities, it goes to the payment of wages,
Cendana said that he will make the motion to restore the CHR’s budget to its full amount at the proper time. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman's proposed 2027 budget clears Senate panel, includes P51.47-M confi funds
articles.summary: The proposed budget of Office of the Ombudsman for 2027, which includes P51.47 million in confidential funds, passed Thursday the scrutiny of the Senate finance committee and has been endorsed for…

blocks.text: The proposed budget of Office of the Ombudsman for 2027, which includes P51.47 million in confidential funds, passed Thursday the scrutiny of the Senate finance committee and has been endorsed for plenary consideration.

Despite concerns over the agency's spending capacity and staffing vacancies, senators expressed support for the Ombudsman's budget. The approval is subject to proposed amendments and the submission of documents requested during the hearing.

The P7.2232-billion figure is the amount recommended by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) for inclusion in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), including automatic appropriations, according to Ombudsman officials.
The amount is substantially lower than the P12.796-billion budget originally proposed by the Ombudsman, leaving a roughly P5.57-billion gap between the agency's request and the DBM recommendation.
Where things stand, the proposed budget represents an increase of about P646 million compared to last year's allocation of P6.577 billion.

Senator Panfilo Lacson said he was "fully supportive" of recommending the Ombudsman's budget to the plenary, while other senators in the finance panel likewise expressing support for strengthening the agency's investigative capacity.
Confidential funds
The P51.468 million allocated for confidential expenses is tabbed under the Ombudsman's maintenance and other operating expenses.
The funds, according to Ombudsman officials, would support the agency's investigation, prosecution and corruption-prevention functions.

During the hearing, Senator Joseph Victor "JV" Ejercito asked about the agency's request for confidential funds, noting that the Ombudsman had sought P148 million, but only about P51 million was included in the DBM-recommended budget.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said the confidential funds would help establish safe quarters for witnesses and, in some instances, marshals, as well as support sensitive investigative activities.

He also cited the Office of the Ombudsman's plan to appoint an Assistant Ombudsman for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), which he said would entail additional security requirements.
"We are more aggressive in pursuing investigations, Your Honor, and pursuing information and other things needed that requires confidential funds to be utilized," Remulla said.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchlian defended the allocation, saying the amount was small compared to the scale of corruption cases being investigated by the Ombudsman.
He said confidential funds could be legitimately used to obtain information needed to strengthen evidence and cases.
Ombudsman asked for P12.8B
The agency's original P12.796-billion proposal included funding for several priorities that were reduced in the DBM recommendation.

Remulla identified the agency's priority items for possible restoration as the purchase of a new office building worth P1.465 billion; more than P167 million for the proposed Ombudsman Marshal Service; additional confidential funds amounting to P148 million; and funds for motor vehicles for officials and general dispatch.
"These are the priority items," Remulla told senators.

Lacson had asked the Ombudsman to identify which programs would be most affected by the DBM cuts and which items should be restored to prevent the reductions from hampering the agency's anti-corruption investigations.
Vacant positions
A major point of discussion was the Ombudsman's request for about P1.68 billion to fill 1,247 vacant plantilla positions.
The agency has more than 2,400 authorized positions, but only about 1,300 personnel are currently filled, translating to a vacancy rate of roughly 51%.
Senator Vicente "Tito" Sotto III questioned why only about half of the agency's plantilla positions were filled.
Remulla said the Ombudsman was already accelerating recruitment, but the government hiring process remained lengthy because of stringent screening requirements.
He said the agency has hired 60 lawyers in 2026 and expects to hire 40 more by November.
According to Remulla, about 3,700 applicants applied for the 100 lawyer positions.
The Ombudsman also cited office-space limitations as another constraint on hiring.
Fund utilization
Lacson, meanwhile, questioned whether the Ombudsman could realistically utilize the full P1.68-billion staffing allocation given its current vacancy rate and hiring pace.
Remulla said the agency could hire more than 400 personnel within another year if given the resources, but acknowledged that filling all the vacancies could take about three years.
He attributed this partly to the office's limited experience in absorbing a substantially larger workforce.
"It's the absorptive capacity of the office," Remulla said.

Lacson suggested that a portion of the proposed staffing allocation could instead be realigned toward the Ombudsman Marshal Service, allowing the agency to prioritize funds it could actually utilize within the two-year period covered by continuing appropriations.
Ombudsman Marshal Service
Ombudsman officials said the proposed Ombudsman Marshal Service would have 100 positions nationwide.
It is intended to complement the Ombudsman's enforcement and investigative functions, including providing protection and security support.
The request drew scrutiny because of the Ombudsman's existing high vacancy rate.
Senators asked how quickly the agency could recruit, vet, and train the proposed marshals to ensure that the additional appropriations would not remain unused.
Budget breakdown
The DBM-recommended P7.2232-billion budget is divided primarily among personnel services, operating expenses and capital outlays:

items: P3.760765 billion for personnel services, or about 52%
P2.444135 billion for maintenance and other operating expenses, or about 33.79%
P857.1 million for capital outlays, or about 11.85%
P2.602 million as the Ombudsman's share in the military camps sales fund, or about 0.04%

blocks.text: The proposed budget also includes P497.549 million for information and communications technology requirements, including modernization of its IT infrastructure.

It also earmarked P11.55 million for the construction of a document storage building for the Ombudsman's Visayas office, citing the need to securely preserve and retrieve case records, evidence files and administrative documents.

Another P95.031 million was retained for the upgrading of depreciated office equipment, furniture and fixtures, while P500 million was recommended as funding support for the purchase of an Ombudsman building under a lease-purchase agreement. — VDV, GMA News
